Examples of previous locations, as well as information on the location and cost of the field course is available from the department in the winter semester prior to each fall offering.
GEOG*4690.Restriction: Restricted to students in BSCH.EG, BAH.EGOV, BAH.GEOG and BSES with an overall average of at least 70% at the time of registration. Instructor consent required.
GEOG*4690.Department: Department of  Geography, Environment and Geomatics
GEOG*4690.Requisites:
12.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

GEOG*4880.Title: GEOG*4880 Contemp Geographic Thought (0.5 Credits)
GEOG*4880.Description: A critical overview of the evolution and current  status of Geography. Particular emphasis will be  given to the variety of approaches and  convergence and divergence within the discipline.  The interaction between human and physical  geographers and their approaches to issues and  the subject will be analyzed.
GEOG*4880.Restriction: Restricted to major honours students in Geography  at semester 6 or above.
GEOG*4880.Department: Department of Geography, Environment and  Geomatics

GEOG*4900.Title: GEOG*4900 Special Topics in Geography (0.5 Credits)
GEOG*4900.Description: In this advanced course, students will investigate issues, patterns, and emerging trends through a geographic lens and/or by gaining experience in one or more methods pertinent to the discipline. Format and topics will vary depending on the instructor's expertise, but the overall themes of the course will relate back to one or more of advanced physical geography, human geography, geographic information science or human-environment geography.
GEOG*4900.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH.GEOG, BAH.EGOV, BSCH.EG, BSES with a minimum 70% cumulative average in all GEOG courses taken.
GEOG*4900.Department: Department of  Geography, Environment and Geomatics
GEOG*4900.Requisites: 12.00 credits   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

GEOG*4990.Title: GEOG*4990 Independent Study in Geography (0.5 Credits)
GEOG*4990.Description: The independent study option is designed to  provide senior undergraduate students with an  opportunity to pursue library or field research  under faculty supervision and to prepare a  research report. Formal agreement between the  student and the faculty supervisor is required,  as is approval of the department chair.
GEOG*4990.Restriction: Restricted to students in BSCH.EG, BSCH.EG:C, BAH.EGOV, BAH.GEOG and BSES with an overall average of at least 70% at the time of registration. Instructor consent required.
GEOG*4990.Department: Department of  Geography, Environment and Geomatics
GEOG*4990.Offered: Summer, Fall, and Winter, All Years

GERM*1100.Title: GERM*1100 Introductory German I (0.5 Credits)
GERM*1100.Description: This is a foundational course in German. Students will attain a basic knowledge of the language and practice all four language skills (listening, speaking, reading and writing). They will also learn about aspects of German culture.
GERM*1100.Offering: Also offered through Distance Education format.
GERM*1100.Restriction: This course is not intended for students with prior knowledge in German. Students with previous knowledge in the language must seek advice on course selection from the Head of the German program and might be assigned to another level of German.

GERM*1110.Title: GERM*1110 Introductory German II (0.5 Credits)
GERM*1110.Description: This course provides for an intensification of  the four language skills introduced in GERM*1100.  Students will attain a grasp of essential  grammatical concepts and the ability to converse  comfortably in everyday situations. This course  may not normally be taken by anyone who has Grade  12U German.
GERM*1110.Requisites:
GERM*1100
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

GERM*2010.Title: GERM*2010 Intermediate Language Practice (0.5 Credits)
GERM*2010.Description: This course provides further practice in the four  skills and in the application of grammatical  concepts.
GERM*2010.Requisites: GERM*2490   - Must be taken either prior to or at the same time as this course.

GERM*2490.Title: GERM*2490 Intermediate German (0.5 Credits)
GERM*2490.Description: This course completes the introduction of  grammatical concepts. It includes systematic oral  and written practice and discussion of texts.
GERM*2490.Requisites:
12U German or GERM*1110
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

GERM*3000.Title: GERM*3000 Narratives of Migration (0.5 Credits)
GERM*3000.Description: This course provides a deeper focus and  additional examples on the topic of HUMN*3000 as  relating to German-speaking countries. It also  involves further oral and written practice in the  German language. Texts will be read in German.
GERM*3000.Requisites:
GERM*2010 or 2.50 credits in German
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
GERM*3000.Locations: HUMN*3000   - Must be taken either prior to or at the same time as this course.

GERM*3020.Title: GERM*3020 Myth & Fairy Tales in Germany (0.5 Credits)
GERM*3020.Description: The course explores the role of mythology, fairy  tales and legends in German literature and  culture. Topics may include the formation of a  national identity, the allegorical fairy tale and  its role in Romanticism, women and the fairy  tale, the fairy tale and the socialization of  children (incl. Disney), adaptations of mythology  in modern literature. Authors may include Goethe,  Brothers Grimm, ETA Hoffmann. Lectures and texts  are in English. Students registered in GERM*3020  will meet a fourth hour per week to discuss texts  in German. This course is offered in parallel with HUMN3020.
GERM*3020.Requisites:
GERM*2010 or 2.50 credits in German
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
GERM*3020.Locations: HUMN*3020   - Must be taken either prior to or at the same time as this course.

GERM*3150.Title: GERM*3150 Interactive German Lang & Cult (0.5 Credits)
GERM*3150.Description: This course develops German language skills and  cultural awareness. Discussions include such  topics as Heimat, nation, migration, and study  abroad. Students will engage with and reflect on  different social and cultural perspectives  through interviews, videos, and texts. Online  interactions, including with people in and from  Germany, form an integral part of the course.
GERM*3150.Offering: Offered through Distance Education  format only.
GERM*3150.Requisites:
GERM*2010 or 2.50 credits in GERM
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

GERM*3470.Title: GERM*3470 Holocaust & WWII/ Germ Lit (0.5 Credits)
GERM*3470.Description: This course focuses on texts and films pertaining  to World War II and the Holocaust, the  development of the thoughts and the language of  genocide, and the representation of the Holocaust  in literature and films. The objective is to gain  an understanding of the ideas and emotions  underlying ethnocentrism and anti-Semitism, and  to consider artistic responses to the experience  of persecution and mass-murder. Lectures and  discussions are in English. Students registered  in GERM*3470 will meet a fourth hour per week to  discuss texts in German. This course is offered  in parallel with HUMN*3470
GERM*3470.Requisites:
GERM*2010 or 2.50 credits in GERM
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
GERM*3470.Locations: HUMN*3470   - Must be taken either prior to or at the same time as this course.

GERM*3600.Title: GERM*3600 Directed Readings in German (0.5 Credits)
GERM*3600.Description: A reading course in German literature designed  according to the program and interest of the  individual student.

GERM*3700.Title: GERM*3700 Experiential Learning & Lang (0.5 Credits)
GERM*3700.Description: This course provides an opportunity for  independent study based on an experiential  project in German. The project (approximately 70  hours) must be approved by a faculty member in  the School of Languages and Literatures. It will  include research about experiential learning, a  reflective piece of writing and a public oral  presentation about the project.
GERM*3700.Restriction: A minimum cumulative average of 70% in all German  course attempts. Instructor consent  required.
GERM*3700.Requisites:
10.00 credits including 1.50 credits in German.
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

GERM*4940.Title: GERM*4940 Research Paper in German Std (0.5 Credits)
GERM*4940.Description: A reading course on some approved topic in German  language or literature, leading to an end-of-term  research paper.

GREK*1100.Title: GREK*1100 Preliminary Greek I (0.5 Credits)
GREK*1100.Description: This is a beginner course in Greek, providing the  fundamentals of structure and idiom. (This course  may not be taken by anyone who has 3U Greek).

GREK*1110.Title: GREK*1110 Preliminary Greek II (0.5 Credits)
GREK*1110.Requisites:
GREK*1100 or 4U Greek
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

GREK*2020.Title: GREK*2020 Greek Language and Culture (0.5 Credits)
GREK*2020.Description: Consolidation of fundamental morphology and  syntax acquired in GREK*1100 and GREK*1110.  Intensive reading in texts that also illuminate  aspects of Greek culture.
GREK*2020.Requisites:
GREK*1110
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*1010.Title: HIST*1010 Early Modern Europe (0.5 Credits)
HIST*1010.Description: This course will deal with the evolution and  expansion of European society during the  pre-industrial era. Commencing with the  Renaissance and Reformation it will survey such  themes as the voyages of exploration, the impact  of western culture on indigenous societies, the  development of commercial capitalism, the  transformation of science and technology and the  conflict between imperial powers in Europe and  overseas.
HIST*1010.Offering: Also offered through  Distance Education format.
HIST*1010.Offered: Summer, Fall, and Winter, All Years

HIST*1050.Title: HIST*1050 Invitation to History (0.5 Credits)
HIST*1050.Description: This course introduces students to the basics of  the historian's craft, including interpreting  primary sources, locating and critically  analyzing secondary sources, and writing for  history. For more detail on the content of  sections consult the History department website.  https://www.uoguelph.ca/history
HIST*1050.Restriction: This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may  be restricted to particular programs and  specializations during certain periods. Please  see the departmental website for more  information.

HIST*1150.Title: HIST*1150 The Modern World (0.5 Credits)
HIST*1150.Description: This course is a survey of the twentieth century,  focusing on major events and themes such as: the  First and Second World Wars, the Great  Depression, the rise and fall of fascism, social  movements, revolutions, genocides, decolonization, nationalism, the Cold War, and the rise and decline of American power. The course draws its examples and case studies mainly from regions across the world, with the intention of broadening critical awareness and fostering global Citizenship.

HIST*1250.Title: HIST*1250 Sci & Tech in a Global Context (0.5 Credits)
HIST*1250.Description: This course is an introduction to the culturally  specific ways in which science and technology  have developed historically from the ancient  period through the twenty-first century. Emphasis  will be placed on the patterns in which  scientific knowledge and practices have traveled  and been constructed across cultures and the  interconnected but distinct histories of science  and technology.

HIST*2000.Title: HIST*2000 The British Isles, 1066 - 1603 (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2000.Description: A comparative survey of the histories of England,  Scotland, Ireland and Wales during the Medieval  and Early Modern eras. Stress will be placed upon  common themes such as institutional development,  warfare and the often violent interaction between  the English and the Celtic peoples.
HIST*2000.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2020.Title: HIST*2020 Film as History (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2020.Description: This course will consider film both as a source  and as a comment on the past. Topics will vary  depending on instructor expertise, and may  include film as propaganda, the city in film,  film as myth, women and gender in film, film and  war. For information on the topic of a specific section, consult the History department website. https://www.uoguelph.ca/history.
HIST*2020.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2040.Title: HIST*2040 War and Society (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2040.Description: Concentrating on developments following the  introduction of gunpowder, the course will  consider the evolution of military strategy and  tactics, the impact of technology on warfare, and  the relationship between war and civilian  populations.
HIST*2040.Offering: Also offered through  Distance Education format.
HIST*2040.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2070.Title: HIST*2070 World Religions (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2070.Description: A wide-ranging look at the diverse religions of  the world including Hinduism, Buddhism, Judaism,  Christianity, and Islam. The course focuses on  each faith's social context and interactions from  their beginnings to the present day.
HIST*2070.Offering: Offered through Distance Education  format only.
HIST*2070.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2090.Title: HIST*2090 Indigenous Peoples - Americas (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2090.Description: This course covers selected events and issues in  Indigenous history in the Americas, including  topics such as origin narratives,  self-governance, intertribal contact,  transatlantic trade, treaty-making, stages of  colonization, Indigenous rights and Indigenous  protest movements. Themes may focus on specific  regions of the Americas and may be examined  through notable Indigenous figures, law and  policy, technology, food, material culture, or  moments of conflict.
HIST*2090.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2100.Title: HIST*2100 Histories of Canada to 1867 (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2100.Description: This course studies political, economic, social, and cultural developments, including the intertwined Indigenous histories, in the lands now known as Canada.
HIST*2100.Requisites: 2.00 credits   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2120.Title: HIST*2120 Animals and Society (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2120.Description: This course provides a historical survey of  modern human-animal relationships and the  contradictions that characterize them. Topics may  include: hunting and sporting, horses and 19th  century cities, natural history and the zoo,  history of veterinary medicine, 20th century  animal sports, the birth of industrial animal  agriculture, animals as biotechnology,  anti-cruelty movements, petkeeping and  consumerism, animal figures in popular culture.  The thematic or geographic focus of the course  may vary according to the expertise of the  instructor.
HIST*2120.Offering: Also offered through  Distance Education format.
HIST*2120.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2130.Title: HIST*2130 Modern Sport - a Global Hist (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2130.Description: Few activities lend themselves more powerfully to  global histories of the modern world than sport.  Since the mid-late nineteenth century, organized  games have become integral parts of mass culture  and everyday life around the world, reflecting  and sometimes shaping much wider political and  socio-economic processes. Encompassing key themes  in the history of the modern world - such as  race, empire, gender, mass media, and nationalism  - this course critically analyzes the development  of modern sport from a global perspective.
HIST*2130.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2160.Title: HIST*2160 9/11 in Historical Perspective (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2160.Description: This course will explore the history of the  moment to understand why 9/11 happened and  examine 9/11's lasting legacy for both the West  and the Arab-Muslim world. It will examine how  the West was historically perceived in the Arab  World, as well as the growth of Islamophobia in  the US, Canada and Europe. This course will  reflect on the intellectual climate of the US and  the Arab world within a historical and political  context often neglected, misunderstood, or  ignored by proponents of the "clash of  civilizations" argument.
HIST*2160.Offering: Offered  through Distance Education format only. Offered  in odd-numbered years.
HIST*2160.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2170.Title: HIST*2170 Context. COVID-19 in History (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2170.Description: The course will examine Covid-19 in historical perspective through lectures from History Faculty on topics including medieval and early modern plagues, the 1918  and other pandemics, the history of vaccination and public health, the rise of hospitals, as well as tourism and sports in times of disruption. Students will create a Covid-19 digital archive, using media, photographs, diaries, and other sources.  They will also be trained in the creation of historical and digital archives and in designing a coherent collection.
HIST*2170.Restriction: This course is restricted to students in HIST programs.

HIST*2180.Title: HIST*2180 Intro to African History (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2180.Description: This course will introduce students to the history of Africa through a chronological examination of key themes and topics from the earliest times until the recent post-independence period. Highlighting the interdisciplinary methodologies that anchor history, the course will consider archeological evidence, oral traditions, historical linguistics, and written documents in its examination of the most significant developments of the African past. These developments will include the creation of modern human culture, early state building efforts, the introduction of Christianity and Islam, the Atlantic Slave trade, colonialism and nationalism, and Africa's relationship with globalization. The course will enable students to develop an understanding of historical factors that have shaped and continue to influence the history of the African continent.
HIST*2180.Requisites: 2.00 credits   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2190.Title: HIST*2190 Celtic Ireland and Britain (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2190.Description: This course will explore the Celts of Ireland and  Britain from the time of the druids to the  post-millennium emergence of literature relating  to a king called Arthur. Reflecting on what we  know of the Celts, how we know it, and what the  term means, the course will examine topics such  as the development of kingdoms and elite 'heroic'  culture, the spread of Christianity, the law,  everyday life and the family, art and literature,  and the interaction between the Celts and their  neighbours.
HIST*2190.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2200.Title: HIST*2200 The Middle Ages (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2200.Description: This course examines many of the major events and developments in medieval Europe from the fall of the Roman Empire to 1500 CE. Important themes include the spread of Christianity, interactions with Islam and Judaism, the emergence of important medieval institutions and relations with the Byzantine Empire and the Eastern Mediterranean.
HIST*2200.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2220.Title: HIST*2220 Buying & Selling: Consumer Cul (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2220.Description: This course explores how the things we buy shape  our personal identities and how individuals  relate to corporations and advertisers, in the  context of the emergence of modern consumer  society from the 18th century to the present. It  critically examines the shift from  home-production economies to mass production.  Examining how developments such as department  stores, product branding, modern advertising,  urbanization, and suburbanization have shaped  society, politics, and the economy, the course  provides a historical context for contemporary  debates about consumer culture.
HIST*2220.Offering: Also offered through Distance Education  format.
HIST*2220.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2240.Title: HIST*2240 Women, War and Nation (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2240.Description: This course is a survey of the inter-connected  nature of gender constructs, nation-states and  violence in history, primarily focused on the  nineteenth and twentieth centuries. The course  proceeds in a roughly chronological order,  examining individuals, nations, revolutions, and  wars across the globe. We engage in individual  and comparative studies to question the gendered  origins and effects of nationalism and violence  in history - and their continuing relevance.
HIST*2240.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2250.Title: HIST*2250 Environment and History (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2250.Description: An introduction to the field of environmental  history - its nature and uses. This course  provides a historical perspective to  environmental issues. It examines the causes and  impact of human-induced modification of the  natural world in selected areas of the globe, the  evolution of attitudes and ideas about the  natural world over time and the growth of  conservation/environmental issues and movements.
HIST*2250.Offering: Also offered through Distance  Education format.
HIST*2250.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2260.Title: HIST*2260 Religion and Society (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2260.Description: This course surveys the major trends in religious  beliefs and practices and their social impact  since the Reformation. The focus of the course is  on the British Isles and North America with some  discussion of developments in Continental Europe.
HIST*2260.Offering: Offered through Distance Education  format only.
HIST*2260.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2280.Title: HIST*2280 Hockey in Canadian History (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2280.Description: Hockey provides a valuable prism through which  major cultural, socio-economic and even political  developments within Canada can be reflected. This  course reviews the considerable role that hockey  has played in Canada's post-Confederation  history. From the late nineteenth century and  throughout the twentieth century, hockey has  helped to inform the nation's sense of self and  has also reflected prevailing social attitudes  and cultural values within Canada.
HIST*2280.Offering: Offered through Distance Education format  only.
HIST*2280.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2300.Title: HIST*2300 The United States Since 1776 (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2300.Description: This course provides a survey of United States  history from the Revolutionary period to the  present. Course lectures, readings and  assignments ask students to interrogate broadly  the social, cultural, economic and political  changes and continuities in America, as well as  the nation's emergence as a superpower.
HIST*2300.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2340.Title: HIST*2340 Slavery & Migr in the Atlantic (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2340.Description: The course will deal with the forced migration of  Africans resulting from the Atlantic slave trade  and the indentured labor migration of Indians to  the Caribbean Isles, the latter which was  associated with the demise of the slave trade and  slavery. Issues to examine will include a  comparison of forces internal and external to  Africa and India productive of the exodus, the  nature of diaspora communities established by the  both set of migrants, and the socio-political and  economic dynamics involved in their establishment  as citizens of their new societies during the  period.
HIST*2340.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2450.Title: HIST*2450 The Practising Historian (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2450.Description: This course is designed to deepen students' understanding of diverse historical primary and secondary sources, advance their practices of historical research and writing, and explore critical interpretive problems surrounding the study of history.
HIST*2450.Requisites:
2.00 credits, including 0.50 credits in History at the 1000  level
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2500.Title: HIST*2500 Britain Since 1603 (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2500.Description: This course will survey the history of England  and the Celtic Regions of the British Isles from  the close of the Tudor period up to the mid-20th  century. Emphasis will be placed on social and  economic development before and after the  Industrial Revolution as well as on those  political and military challenges which have  characterized Britain's status as a global power  in the modern era.
HIST*2500.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2510.Title: HIST*2510 Modern Europe Since 1789 (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2510.Description: This course will deal with the emergence of  modern European society as the result of  socio-economic and consequent political changes  from the French Revolution, through the World  Wars, to the collapse of communism and the  formation of the European Union.
HIST*2510.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2600.Title: HIST*2600 Histories of Canada Since 1867 (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2600.Description: This course studies political, economic, social, and cultural developments in post-Confederation Canadian history, including the intertwined histories of Indigenous peoples.
HIST*2600.Requisites: 2.00 credits   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2820.Title: HIST*2820 Modern France Since 1750 (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2820.Description: This course is a survey of French history from  the beginning of modernization in the 18th  century to the challenges of the late 20th  century. Topics will include the Revolution, the  Napoleonic period, social and political  transformation in the 19th century, the Great  War, the defeat of 1940 and Vichy, and the  remarkable changes in French life since the  Second World War.
HIST*2820.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2850.Title: HIST*2850 Ancient Greece and Rome (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2850.Description: The history of the Mediterranean World from  prehistoric Greece through Classical Greece and  Rome to the legalization of Christianity in the  Roman Empire in the 4th century will be covered  in this course.
HIST*2850.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2890.Title: HIST*2890 Early Islamic World (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2890.Description: This course is an introduction to the history of  Islam. The course will consider the founding of  Islam, and its global diffusion, from the seventh  to the fourteenth centuries.
HIST*2890.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2910.Title: HIST*2910 Modern Asia (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2910.Description: An introduction to the histories and cultures of  Asia since 1750. This course will consider the  evolution of Asian religions, cultural  identities, concepts of state and of society in  the modern era.
HIST*2910.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2920.Title: HIST*2920 Republican Latin America (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2920.Description: This course will study selected themes in the  history of Latin American republics from the  independence period to the modern era.
HIST*2920.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*2930.Title: HIST*2930 Women and Cultural Change (0.5 Credits)
HIST*2930.Description: Using gender and ethnicity as the main categories  of analysis, this course examines the history of  women within one global geographical region such  as Asia, South America and the Caribbean or North  America. The roles women have played in  political, economic and private life will be  emphasized.
HIST*2930.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3020.Title: HIST*3020 Sexuality & Gender in History (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3020.Description: This course provides an introduction to the  issues of sexuality and gender within history.  The course will enable students to develop an  understanding of how issues of masculinity,  femininity, and sexuality were developed and  defined across cultures. The chronological and  geographic focus of the course may vary according  to the interests and expertise of the instructor.
HIST*3020.Requisites: 7.50 credits including 0.50 credits in History, (1 of 0.50 credits in History, PHIL*2060, POLS*2150, SOAN*2400, WMST*1000, WMST*2000)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
HIST*3020.Locations: 7.50 credits including 0.50 credits in History, (1 of 0.50 credits in History, PHIL*2060, POLS*2150, SOAN*2400, WMST*1000, WMST*2000)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3070.Title: HIST*3070 Modern India (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3070.Description: This course studies the history of modern India  from 1757 to the present day. Topics include:  European and British imperialism in India, Indian  reactions to imperialism, socio-religious  movements, the birth of nationalism and the  nation-state in India, civil society and social  issues in a developing nation, regionalism,  foreign policy and India's place in the 21st  century.
HIST*3070.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3080.Title: HIST*3080 United States in the World (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3080.Description: This course is a study of the United States as a  global phenomenon. Thematic topics will go beyond  foreign policy and military history to include  imperialism, immigration, globalization, race,  gender, ethnicity, consumption, tourism, and  international cultural industries.
HIST*3080.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3130.Title: HIST*3130 Popular Culture and Punishment (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3130.Description: The course will survey the social, political and  intellectual influences upon the leisure  activities of Europeans and Americans in the  period with special reference to institutions  such as the prison, the asylum, the reformatory  and the regulation of popular culture and leisure  activities. Witchcraft and the witch-hunt will be  discussed.
HIST*3130.Offering: Also offered through  Distance Education format.
HIST*3130.Requisites:
7.50 credits including (HIST*1010 or SOC*1500)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3140.Title: HIST*3140 Witch-Hunts & Popular Culture (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3140.Description: This course will explore the phenomenon of the  'witch-hunts' in early modern Europe through a  focus on Scotland in the period 1560-1700. In  addition to placing the witch-hunts in their  historical context by providing students with the  background to Scotland's political, religious,  and social history in the early modern period,  the course will introduce students to the  considerable body of historical writing on the  subject of the witch-hunts and give them hands on  experience with primary source documents in order  to discuss specific witch trials themselves.  Popular and elite conceptions of witchcraft will  be explored, as well as gender history.
HIST*3140.Offering: Offered through Distance Education  format only.
HIST*3140.Requisites: 7.50 credits   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3150.Title: HIST*3150 History and Culture of Mexico (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3150.Description: This course will cover the history and culture of  Mexico from its Pre-columbian civilizations to the present. Topics may include: Aztec and Mayan  civilizations, European discovery and conquest,  inquisition, convents, independence, the Mexican  revolution, indigenismo, NAFTA and Zapatista  insurgency in Chiapas.
HIST*3150.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3160.Title: HIST*3160 Political & Policy History (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3160.Description: This course examines the development of Canadian political life and public policy from Confederation to the early 21st century. It takes a broad approach to its understanding of politics, including traditional elements such as elections, political parties, federalism and leadership. It also considers the diverse array of actors and forces that have shaped policy and political culture in Canada, including social movement activism, transnational influences, and factors such as gender, class, race/ethnicity, religion and language. Significant attention is paid to the development of public policy, including social welfare policy, foreign policy and identity policies such as official languages and multiculturalism.
HIST*3160.Requisites: 7.50 credits   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3180.Title: HIST*3180 Canada Since 1945 (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3180.Description: This course provides an in-depth examination of  political, social, cultural, and economic changes  in Canada since the Second World War. Particular  attention will be paid to the increased diversity  of the Canadian population, the development of  Canadian institutions, and the changing role  played by Canada in the world.
HIST*3180.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3200.Title: HIST*3200 Youth in History (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3200.Description: This course examines the social history of  childhood, youth and adolescence in western  culture and how life-cycles vary as a function of  class, race and ethnicity, gender and sexuality.  It will examine the experiences of young people  in different historical eras. Questions to be  explored include: Does the notion of adolescence  transcend history and culture? How have experts  constructed institutions such as the high school,  the juvenile justice system, the media, medical  and social scientific research to channel youth  rebellion? Historical case studies will be  selected to show generations in political,  community and domestic conflict. This  interdisciplinary history course draws upon  sociology, anthropology, cultural studies, art,  music, literature, academic writing and research  from Europe, Canada and the United States.
HIST*3200.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3230.Title: HIST*3230 Spain & Portugal, 1085-1668 (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3230.Description: The course examines the history of Spain and  Portugal from the period of the reconquista to  overseas expansion. The course covers the  political, diplomatic, religious and cultural  development of early modern Spain and Portugal  and the rise of the overseas empire.
HIST*3230.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3240.Title: HIST*3240 Food History (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3240.Description: This course will examine the history of food and  foodways from the early 19th century to the  present. It will explore the impact of changing  agricultural practices and the growth of the food  processing industry, including the rise of  nutritional science, and the impact on eating  patterns.
HIST*3240.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3260.Title: HIST*3260 Cinema & the Moving Image (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3260.Description: This course provides a historical survey of  cinema and the moving image, as well as the  material, cultural, political and technological  contexts of their production. Students will come  to understand the broad development of the medium  over the past one hundred and thirty years,  beginning with early, pre-cinematic moving image  technologies and ending with an analysis of the  influence of other media and merchandizing on  cinema. Students will also become familiar with  crucial terminology for analyzing and writing  about how films have been constructed and how  they communicated to audiences over time.  Geographic or thematic focus may vary according  to the expertise of the instructor.
HIST*3260.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3270.Title: HIST*3270 Revolution in the Modern World (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3270.Description: This course offers a comparative analysis of  revolutionary movements in the modern world. It  focuses on the French Revolution, the development  of a revolutionary tradition in the 19th century,  the Russian Revolution, and the Communist  Revolution in China. Comparative themes include  the relative importance of ideology and class  conflict, the emergence of professional  revolutionaries, and the relationship between  revolutions and international relations.
HIST*3270.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3310.Title: HIST*3310 Disease and History (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3310.Description: This interdisciplinary course provides an  introduction to the historical interactions  between disease and human society from the Middle  Ages to the present. Major themes may include the  co-construction of disease and society; disease  and urbanization; disease and colonialism;  disease and globalization; disease and gender.
HIST*3310.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3320.Title: HIST*3320 Modern China (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3320.Description: This course examines the history and culture of  China since the nineteenth century. Topics may  include economics, gender, imperialism,  militarism, politics, and religion.
HIST*3320.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3330.Title: HIST*3330 The Scottish Diaspora (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3330.Description: The course offers a comprehensive overview of  Scottish Diaspora history, focusing on a broad  range of themes and settlement locations.  Covering the period c.1750 to 1945, the  historical geographies of the Scottish Diaspora  explored include the 'near Diaspora' of England,  Wales and Ireland; Continental Europe; the  traditional settler Dominions; the United States;  Africa; and Asia.
HIST*3330.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3350.Title: HIST*3350 Modern Germany (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3350.Description: This course will be devoted to a study of major  themes in modern German history, and to an  analysis of Germany's role in post-war Europe.  Topics include the unification of Germany, the  role of nationalism in modern German history, the  significance of the Bismarck era, the rise of  Hitler and the development of the two Germanies  until their unification in 1990.
HIST*3350.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3360.Title: HIST*3360 History and Culture of Brazil (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3360.Description: This course will cover the history and culture of  Brazil from its early indigenous civilizations to  the present. Topics may include: European  discovery and contact, the colonial era, slave  trade and slavery, Dutch occupation, hybrid  Afro-Christian religions, the Inquisition,  independence, abolitionism, samba and carnival,  dictatorships, soccer, favelas, and issues  related to race, class, gender and the  environment.
HIST*3360.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3370.Title: HIST*3370 Canada and the First World War (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3370.Description: This course examines Canada's role in the First  World War. The question of how much the war was a  transformative experience for Canadians will be  central to students' learning, as they grapple  with issues pertaining to race, ethnicity, class,  gender, militarism, pacifism, religion, age, and  memory.
HIST*3370.Offering: Offered through Distance  Education format only.
HIST*3370.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3380.Title: HIST*3380 British Imper in Asia & Africa (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3380.Description: This course examines the British Empire from the  18th through the 20th centuries. It focuses on:  the empire in Asia and Africa; ideologies of  empire; and European and non-European approaches  and reactions to empire.
HIST*3380.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3390.Title: HIST*3390 Govt & Indigenous Spaces (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3390.Description: This course examines how colonial and  neo-colonial governments interacted with  Indigenous societies by restricting social,  economic, and cultural activities. It will  explore the day-to-day impacts of colonial and  neo-colonial governments on Indigenous spaces.  Engagement with case studies will deepen student  understanding of both bureaucratic violence and  Indigenous survivance.
HIST*3390.Requisites:
7.50 credits including (1.00 credits in History or  IDEV*2400)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
HIST*3390.Locations:
7.50 credits including (1.00 credits in History or  IDEV*2400)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3440.Title: HIST*3440 The Global Sixties (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3440.Description: This course examines the political, social, and  cultural history of one of the most important  decades in the twentieth century: the sixties. It  adopts global perspectives to ask how and why the  sixties mattered in the development of the modern  world. A diverse range of themes may be covered,  from the political controversies stirred up by  the Vietnam War, decolonisation in Africa, Mao's  cultural revolution, the Cuban missile crisis,  and the upheavals of 1968 to the social changes  occasioned by the introduction of the birth  control pill, the rise of The Beatles, and the  emergence of television.
HIST*3440.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3450.Title: HIST*3450 Public History and Society (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3450.Description: As an introduction to the public use of historical knowledge, this course discusses public history, memory, and commemoration through the activities of governments, corporations, and voluntary associations. It explores how historical knowledge has been used and mis-used. History as political propaganda, marketing strategy, and ideological support in a global and historical context is examined.
HIST*3450.Requisites: 7.50 credits including HIST*2450    - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3460.Title: HIST*3460 Disasters in Global History (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3460.Description: The history of natural disasters offers insights  into how the relationships between human  societies and their natural environments have  changed over time. Through a series of case  studies, the course will trace the evolving  history of natural disasters in global context  from the late medieval period to the present. The  course will address thematic issues including the  construction of vulnerable landscapes and  societies; the short-term impacts of disasters;  changing patterns of disaster relief; and  disasters and social change.
HIST*3460.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3470.Title: HIST*3470 Ind Reading/Workplace Learning (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3470.Description: A course of independent study, based on a reading list agreed upon by the instructor and the student. Students interested in this course should approach prospective instructors directly to determine their willingness to act as supervisor.
HIST*3470.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3480.Title: HIST*3480 Workplace Learning (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3480.Description: An independent study course based on either  History related voluntary or paid workplace  experience. Evaluation will be based on  assignments relating to work duties. These will  usually be in the form of a weekly journal, and a  major project relating to some specific aspect of  the work experience. Students interested in this  option must have their project approved by the  department prior to the semester in which they  plan to engage in their work experience. Students  will then be assigned to a faculty supervisor who  will oversee the project.
HIST*3480.Requisites: 7.50 credits including 1.50 History credits   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3490.Title: HIST*3490 Canada & the Second World War (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3490.Description: This course examines Canada's experience with the  Second World War. Topics include: Canada's  changing roles in the world; the role and growth  of the state; gender and sexuality; conscription  and English-French relations; race, ethnicity and  the experiences of Indigenous peoples during the  war; the homefront and social transformations;  military engagements and soldier experiences;  nationalisms, citizenship and identity; wartime  legacies and post-war ramifications; public  history and the memory of the war.
HIST*3490.Offering: Also offered through Distance Education.  Offered in odd-numbered years.
HIST*3490.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3520.Title: HIST*3520 The Vikings (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3520.Description: This course explores the topic of the Vikings in  early medieval culture (700 - 1100). The focus  will include the role of violence in early  medieval society, the construction of the  'Other', as well as medieval and modern  historiography. It provides students with  enhanced knowledge of early medieval Europe, the  Byzantine Empire and Russia.
HIST*3520.Requisites:
7.50 credits including (HIST*2000 or HIST*2200)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3560.Title: HIST*3560 Experiential Learning (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3560.Description: This course combines scholarly research and  self-reflection with applied experience in a  History-related workplace or simulated workplace  environment. Students apply and develop their  program-based historical skills and knowledge  through in-class learning and a project with a  local community partner organization. The project  is designed to contribute to a public body of  knowledge and improve students' skills for the  workplace.
HIST*3560.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3570.Title: HIST*3570 Women in Modern Europe (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3570.Description: This course will examine selected topics in  modern European women's history. Attention will  be given to action in the public sphere, women's  personal and family lives and occupations.
HIST*3570.Requisites:
7.50 credits including (1 of HIST*2500, HIST*2510,  HIST*2800, HIST*2930)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3580.Title: HIST*3580 Women's History in Asia (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3580.Description: This course examines the roles of women in one or  more countries of Asia through the prisms offered  by ideas of 'race', class, gender, social status,  material culture, intellectual life, and  ideology.
HIST*3580.Requisites:
7.50 credits including (1 of HIST*1150, HIST*2240,  HIST*2890, HIST*2910, HIST*2930)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3590.Title: HIST*3590 Ancient & Medieval India (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3590.Description: This course examines the history of India from  the beginnings of civilization on the Indian  subcontinent to the end of the Great Mughals in  the 18th century. It provides an overview and  analysis of the cultural, social, religious,  political and economic development of Indian  civilization, including development from tribe to  state to civil society, political organization,  socio-religious movements, cultural contact and  exchange, and the development of a composite  culture.
HIST*3590.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3600.Title: HIST*3600 Quebec & French Canada (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3600.Description: This course examines selected themes in the  social, economic, political and cultural  evolution of Quebec and its relations with the  rest of Canada. The course may also examine the  development of French Canadian and Acadian  communities in other provinces.
HIST*3600.Requisites: 7.50 credits   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3610.Title: HIST*3610 History of Modern Tourism (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3610.Description: This course examines the history of the travel and tourism industry and its social, political, and cultural impacts from the rise of the European Grand Tour in the 18th century to the present day. Aspects of tourism history to be covered may include the development of the business of tourism, improvements in travel technology, hotels and accommodations, developing destinations, marketing in historical perspective, and interactions between travelers and host societies.
HIST*3610.Requisites: 7.50 credits   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3620.Title: HIST*3620 Modern Africa (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3620.Description: The course will explore the crucial experiences of African societies from the ending of the Atlantic slave trade until the recent past. It will focus on African peoples' interactions with each other and with the expanding forces of global capitalism and European colonialism and on their struggle for political independence. It will also examine Africa's more recent post-colonial experiences of the politics of nation-building and state formation and the struggle for economic development. It will give attention to African agency and to the internal historical dynamics within the continent even as its peoples grappled with the global social, economic, political, and cultural currents that impacted them during this period.
HIST*3620.Requisites: 7.50 credits   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3640.Title: HIST*3640 Madness and Psychiatry (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3640.Description: This course will explore madness and the history  of psychiatry in the modern world. Topics may  include the development of asylums, wild children  and human nature, the rise and fall of hysteria,  psychoanalysis, as well as ways in which  psychiatry has related to imperialism, racial  policies, sexuality, gender, religious beliefs,  and war.
HIST*3640.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3660.Title: HIST*3660 Canadian Social History (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3660.Description: This course examines selected themes in the  development of Canadian society such as the role  of class, the social consequences of  industrialization and urbanization, immigration,  ethnicity and religion, education and culture.
HIST*3660.Requisites: 7.50 credits   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3690.Title: HIST*3690 Darwin, Culture and Society (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3690.Description: This course will focus on the historical, social,  and cultural dimensions of Darwin's theory of  evolution, from the late 18th century to the  present. Topics may include: natural history,  classification, social Darwinism, race and  imperialism, science & religion, science &  literature, the eugenics movement, the Scopes  trial, the modern evolutionary synthesis,  sociobiology, gender, antievolutionism and  creationism/intelligent design.
HIST*3690.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3700.Title: HIST*3700 Race, Immigration in N.America (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3700.Description: This course explores the history of race and immigration in North America with an emphasis on Canada and the United States, beginning with early contact between Indigenous nations and Europeans and extending into the twenty-first century. The course will teach students about the historically changing nature of race and immigration through a variety of themes such as colonialism, slavery, gender, and politics.
HIST*3700.Requisites: 7.50 credits   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3750.Title: HIST*3750 The Reformation (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3750.Description: The changes in religious, social and cultural  life in 16th century Europe will be discussed.  This course will examine the impact of humanism,  the developments in urban culture known as the  Renaissance, the reform movements in central and  western Europe, the Catholic response, and the  resulting disintegration of the medieval social  order.
HIST*3750.Requisites:
7.50 credits including HIST*1010
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3820.Title: HIST*3820 Early Modern France (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3820.Description: This course surveys French History from the  Renaissance to the French Revolution. Students  will examine the emergence of the powerful  monarchy, 16th-century religious conflict and  civil war, and the social, political and  intellectual developments of the 17th and 18th  centuries, which culminated in the 1789  Revolution.
HIST*3820.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3830.Title: HIST*3830 Modern Middle East (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3830.Description: This course explores struggles for national  independence in the region after 1919, the impact  of the developing oil industry, the creation of  Israel and the resulting Arab-Israeli conflict,  the rise of American influence, the divisiveness  of Cold War politics, and the role of women in  contemporary Islamic societies.
HIST*3830.Requisites: 7.50 credits including (1 of HIST*1150, HIST*2890, HIST*3840, POLS*3060)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3840.Title: HIST*3840 Ottoman Empire, 1300-1923 (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3840.Description: This course examines the rise of the Ottoman  Empire in the 14th century, both in Europe and  the Middle East, and traces its evolution until  its demise in the 20th century. Students  investigate the historiographical debates  surrounding various aspects of writing Ottoman  history.
HIST*3840.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3960.Title: HIST*3960 Experiential Learning II (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3960.Description: This course combines scholarly research and self-reflection with applied experience in a History-related workplace or simulated workplace environment. Students apply and develop their program-based historical skills and knowledge through in-class learning and a project with a local community partner organization. The project is designed to contribute to a public body of knowledge and improve students' skills for the workplace. This course is intended for students who have already taken HIST*3560, and wish to take a second Experiential Learning course under a different course code.
HIST*3960.Requisites: HIST*3560   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*3980.Title: HIST*3980 Workplace Learning II (0.5 Credits)
HIST*3980.Description: An independent study course based on either History related voluntary or paid workplace experience. Evaluation will be based on assignments relating to work duties. These will usually be in the form of a weekly journal, and a major project relating to some specific aspect of the work experience. Students interested in this option must have their project approved by the department prior to the semester in which they plan to engage in their work experience. Students will then be assigned to a faculty supervisor who will oversee the project. This course is for students who have already completed a workplace learning course using the course code HIST*3480 and wish to do a second one.
HIST*3980.Requisites: HIST*3480   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4010.Title: HIST*4010 Gender and Culture (1 Credits)
HIST*4010.Description: This course will examine how masculinity and  femininity has been constructed in popular  culture using newspapers, magazines,  advertisements, films and novels. Careful  attention will be paid to the intersections of  gender, race and class. In addition to analyzing  some outstanding texts in this field, students  will have the opportunity to write an original  essay on a topic of their choice.
HIST*4010.Restriction: Restricted to students in  the BA Honours program with a minimum of 70%  average in all History course  attempts.
HIST*4010.Requisites:
10.00 credits including 1.50 credits in History at the  3000-level
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4030.Title: HIST*4030 Historical Biography (1 Credits)
HIST*4030.Description: This advanced research seminar asks students to  consider the role of the individual in history by  reading theoretical works and examples drawn from  the major schools of thought on this issue.  Students will undertake to write a biography that  will utilize primary sources and will include a  detailed historiographical discussion of the  works available on their chosen subject.
HIST*4030.Restriction: Restricted to students in the  BA Honours program with a minimum of 70% average in all History course attempts.
HIST*4030.Requisites:
10.00 credits including 1.50 credits in History at the  3000-level
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4040.Title: HIST*4040 Topics in Scottish History (1 Credits)
HIST*4040.Description: This is a seminar course dealing with selected aspects of Scottish social, economic and political history. The seminars will be based upon an examination of primary sources from the University library's extensive Scottish Collections, as well as secondary literature. Topics chosen will vary with expertise of the instructor. For information on the topic of a specific section, consult the History department website. https://www.uoguelph.ca/.
HIST*4040.Restriction: Restricted to students in the BA Honours  program with a minimum of 70% average in all  History course attempts.
HIST*4040.Requisites:
10.00 credits including 1.50 credits in History at the  3000-level
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4070.Title: HIST*4070 Experiential Learning-Research (1 Credits)
HIST*4070.Description: This course offers an opportunity for students to  independently develop skills in the practice of  historical research, such as working with  archives, digitization, and database management.  Students will work under the supervision of  individual faculty members. Students must make  arrangements with the faculty advisor well before  course selection.
HIST*4070.Restriction: Restricted  to students in the BA Honours program with a  minimum of 70% average in all History course  attempts. Instructor consent required.
HIST*4070.Requisites:
10.00 credits including 1.50 credits in History at the  3000-level
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4080.Title: HIST*4080 Indigenous Resistance (1 Credits)
HIST*4080.Description: This course explores both individual and  collective acts of Indigenous resistance in  settler-colonial societies. Diverse forms of  resistance will be studied from text-based to  action-based movements. Resistance may be  examined through notable figures, delegations,  marches, occupations, and literature.
HIST*4080.Restriction: Restricted to students in the  BA Honours program with a minimum of 70%  average in all History course attempts.
HIST*4080.Requisites:
10.00 credits including 1.50 credits in History at the  3000-level
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
HIST*4080.Locations:
10.00 credits including 1.50 credits in History at the  3000-level
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4100.Title: HIST*4100 Africa & the Slave Trades (1 Credits)
HIST*4100.Description: This course will discuss the origins, character,  and operation of slavery and the export slave  trades in Africa. It will examine the interaction  between domestic slavery and the export slave  trades, on the one hand, and demographic,  political, economic, social and cultural impact  on African states and societies, on the other.  Other themes to be examined include slave  resistance in Africa, and abolition and the  introduction of legitimate commerce and their  impact on Africa.
HIST*4100.Restriction: Restricted  to students in the BA Honours program with a  minimum of 70% average in all History course  attempts.
HIST*4100.Requisites: 10.00 credits including 1.00 credits in History at the 3000 level   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4120.Title: HIST*4120 Topics in Global History (1 Credits)
HIST*4120.Description: This course focuses on issues that emphasize the  history of connections between different parts of  the world. Topics may include the growth of the  world economy; transformations of the global  environment; trade and exchange; diasporas and  migration. Topics chosen will vary with expertise of the instructor. For information on the topic of a specific section, consult the History department website. https://www.uoguelph.ca/history
HIST*4120.Restriction: Restricted to students in the BA Honours program with a minimum of 70% average in all History course attempts.
HIST*4120.Requisites:
10.00 credits including 1.50 credits in History at the  3000-level
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4140.Title: HIST*4140 Sexuality in the Middle Ages (1 Credits)
HIST*4140.Description: This course will provide a thematic approach to  the foundations of western attitudes towards sex  and sexuality as they developed in the European  Middle Ages. It will examine the complex  interweaving of Greek and Roman medicine,  medieval Christian canon law and theology, and  Germanic popular beliefs, which together provided  the underpinnings of western values and practices  pertaining to human sex and sexuality, with  enduring results. The course will take an  historiographical approach to topics and themes.
HIST*4140.Restriction: Restricted to students in  the BA Honours program with a minimum of 70%  average in all History course attempts.
HIST*4140.Requisites:
10.00 credits including (1 of HIST*2000, HIST*2200,  HIST*3020)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4160.Title: HIST*4160 Activism and Political Change (1 Credits)
HIST*4160.Description: This seminar examines Canadian political history through the lens of the social movements, interest groups and civil society actors that have sought to implement social and political change. Students will consider case studies of social movements focused on various political causes (such as the women's movement, organized labour, Indigenous rights, environmentalism, LGBTQ activism), paying attention to their strategies and tactics for accomplishing political change, their internal dynamics and mobilization of resources, their transnational dimensions, and their impacts on Canadian society.
HIST*4160.Restriction: Restricted to students in the BA Honours program with a minimum of 70% average in all History course attempts.
HIST*4160.Requisites:
10.00 credits including (HIST*2100 or HIST*2600)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4170.Title: HIST*4170 Digital Humanities (1 Credits)
HIST*4170.Description: This course is designed to introduce students to  applications of new and inter-disciplinary  digital humanities approaches, methodologies and  tools, and to explore their application to text,  image, sound, map, and other media sources. It  will appeal to students in literature, history,  fine arts, and music who want an introduction to  state-of-the-art digital humanities research.  There will be flexibility to accommodate the  specific disciplines and interests of the  students.
HIST*4170.Restriction: Restricted to  students in the BA Honours program with a  minimum of 70% average in all History course  attempts.
HIST*4170.Requisites:
10.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4180.Title: HIST*4180 American Identities (1 Credits)
HIST*4180.Description: This course analyzes how Americans have  constructed and enacted identities in the U.S. as  citizens and consumers through investigating  concepts such as 'race', ethnicity, gender,  sexuality, class, regional distinctions, and  nationalism.
HIST*4180.Restriction: HIST*4210.  Restricted to students in the BA Honours  program with a minimum of 70% average in all  History course attempts.
HIST*4180.Requisites: 10.00 credits including 1.50 credits in History at the 3000-level   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4200.Title: HIST*4200 Health, Mind and Body (1 Credits)
HIST*4200.Description: This is a seminar course which will explore the  history of health, the body and the mind.  Possible topics include: the history of athletics  and physical fitness, the history of disability,  the history of nutritional science and advice,  the history of women's health, the history of  disease, the history of mental illness, and the  history of psychiatry.
HIST*4200.Restriction: Restricted to students in the BA Honours  program with a minimum of 70% average in all  History course attempts.
HIST*4200.Requisites:
10.00 credits, including 1.50 credits in History at the  3000-level
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4220.Title: HIST*4220 Cities and Canadian Culture (1 Credits)
HIST*4220.Description: Reflecting the fact that Canada's population has  been predominantly urban for a century, this  seminar explores the role of urban centres in  shaping Canadian cultural identity. Particular  focus will be placed on the ways that city living  and city form have affected the expression of  Canadian identity through such topics as  spectator sports, uses of public spaces, and  metropolitan control of print and broadcast media.
HIST*4220.Restriction: Restricted to students in  the BA Honours program with a minimum of 70%  average in all History course attempts.
HIST*4220.Requisites:
10.00 credits including (HIST*2100 or HIST*2600)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4230.Title: HIST*4230 Histories of Travel & Tourism (1 Credits)
HIST*4230.Description: This is a seminar course exploring the history of travel and tourism.  The seminar will discuss the political, social, cultural, and economic implications of tourism, mobilities, and the interactions of travelers and hosts.  The historical development of the business of tourism will also be discussed.  The seminar may focus on particular periods of history, tourism in specific locations, or particular aspects of the tourism industry.
HIST*4230.Restriction: Restricted to students in the BA Honours program with a minimum of 70% average in all History course attempts.
HIST*4230.Requisites: 10 credits   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4250.Title: HIST*4250 Topics in Enviro History (1 Credits)
HIST*4250.Description: This seminar in environmental history will discuss the historical relationships between humanity and the non-human world by analyzing their political, economic, social, cultural, and ecological implications over time. Topics will vary, but may include issues such as climate change, energy, animals, commodities, resources, food, colonialism, pollution, environmentalism, biodiversity, warfare, and science and technology.
HIST*4250.Restriction: Restricted to students in the BA Honours or BAS program with a minimum of 70% average in all History course attempts.
HIST*4250.Requisites: 10.00 credits including 1.50 credits at the 3000-level in HIST or ASCI   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4270.Title: HIST*4270 Topics in Modern Asia (1 Credits)
HIST*4270.Description: This course will examine select topics in the  development of Asian countries from the 18th to  the 21st Century. Select themes including  imperialism, nationalism, economics, society, and  gender will be examined in a variety of Asian  countries.
HIST*4270.Requisites:
10.00 credits including HIST*2910.
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4280.Title: HIST*4280 Poverty & Policy in Victorian (1 Credits)
HIST*4280.Description: Starting with the debates over the New Poor Law  of 1834, this course will examine the changing  content of the notion of poverty, and changing  methods adopted to treat it. It will also look at  the lives of the poor, in so far as these can be  reconstructed from contemporary sources.
HIST*4280.Restriction: Restricted to students in the  BA Honours program with a minimum of 70%  average in all History course attempts.
HIST*4280.Requisites:
10.00 credits including HIST*2500.
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4450.Title: HIST*4450 Life, Death and Migrations (1 Credits)
HIST*4450.Description: This seminar uses quantitative sources and  methods to explore such themes as social  inequality and demographic experience since 1800.  It examines the value of such data for policy  purposes, as well as the social and cultural  contexts in which surveys are developed and  undertaken. Students develop presentational and  analytical skills through research projects.
HIST*4450.Restriction: Restricted to students in the  BA Honours program with a minimum of 70%  average in all History course attempts.
HIST*4450.Requisites:
10.00 credits including HIST*2450, and at least 1.00  credits in History at the 3000 level or above.
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4470.Title: HIST*4470 Special Hist Proj Seminar I (0.5 Credits)
HIST*4470.Description: This course is designed to train honours students  in the techniques of research, interpretation and  writing of history. The student will choose a topic for intensive study in consultation with an instructor who has agreed to supervise their research.
HIST*4470.Restriction: Restricted  to students in the BA Honours program with a  minimum of 70% average in all History course  attempts. Instructor consent  required.
HIST*4470.Requisites:
10.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4580.Title: HIST*4580 The French Revolution (1 Credits)
HIST*4580.Description: This seminar course provides an in-depth analysis  of the French Revolution, 1789-1799, and the  literature surrounding its interpretation.
HIST*4580.Restriction: Restricted to students in the  BA Honours program with a minimum of 70%  average in all History course attempts.
HIST*4580.Requisites:
10.00 credits including (1 of HIST*2510, HIST*2820,  HIST*3270, HIST*3820)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4620.Title: HIST*4620 Sem in Canadian Rural History (1 Credits)
HIST*4620.Description: This course will examine selected topics in the  social and economic transformation of rural  Canada with relevant comparisons to the rest of  North America and elsewhere.
HIST*4620.Restriction: Restricted to students in the BA Honours  program with a minimum of 70% average in all  History course attempts.
HIST*4620.Requisites: 10.00 credits   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4700.Title: HIST*4700 Premodern History (1 Credits)
HIST*4700.Description: This course provides a detailed analysis of selected aspects of the Middle Ages from c. 1000 C.E. through the early modern period. Topics chosen will vary with expertise of the instructor. For information on the topic of a specific section, consult the History department website. https://www.uoguelph.ca/history
HIST*4700.Restriction: Restricted to students in the BA Honours program with a minimum of 70% average in all History course attempts.
HIST*4700.Requisites:
10.00 credits including HIST*2000 or HIST*2200
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4820.Title: HIST*4820 Reps, Conflict & Politics (1 Credits)
HIST*4820.Description: This seminar will examine select topics in the history, cultural representations, conflicts, and politics of the region known as the 'Middle East,' from the pre-Islamic to the modern era.
HIST*4820.Restriction: Restricted to students in the BA Honours program with a minimum of 70% average in all History course attempts.
HIST*4820.Requisites:
10.00 credits, (1 of HIST*2890, HIST*3830, HIST*3840,  POLS*3060)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HIST*4970.Title: HIST*4970 Special Hist Proj Seminar II (0.5 Credits)
HIST*4970.Description: This course is designed to train honours students in the techniques of research, interpretation and writing of history. The student will choose a topic for intensive study in consultation with an instructor who has agreed to supervise their research. It may be a continuation of HIST*4470 or a new research project.
HIST*4970.Restriction: Restricted to students in the BA Honours  program with a minimum of 70% average in all  History course attempts. Instructor consent  required.
HIST*4970.Requisites: 10.00 credits including HIST*4470   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HK*2270.Title: HK*2270 Human Biomechanics (0.5 Credits)
HK*2270.Description: This course will address the application of  mechanical principles to the study of human  movement. Topics will include: motion analysis  techniques, anthropometrics, biological tissue  tolerance, muscle force generation, static and  dynamic equilibrium, work/energy and  impulse/momentum as they apply to the description  of motion, injury of musculoskeletal tissues and  optimization of human performance.
HK*2270.Department: Department of Human Health and  Nutritional Sciences
HK*2270.Requisites:
4.00 credits including BIOL*1090, PHYS*1080
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HK*2810.Title: HK*2810 Human Physiology I (0.5 Credits)
HK*2810.Description: This course will introduce the fundamental  concepts and principles of communication systems  (transport, ion movement, nerve and synapse,  muscle) in humans. It will focus on primary  physiological communication systems, such as the  endocrine and central nervous systems, and  integrate basic principles to understand larger  systems such as the gastrointestinal tract.
HK*2810.Department: Department of Human Health and  Nutritional Sciences
HK*2810.Requisites:
BIOC*2580, BIOL*1080
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HK*3100.Title: HK*3100 Neuromuscular Physiology (0.5 Credits)
HK*3100.Description: Normal muscle movement is controlled by the motor  cortex or by reflexes within the context of the  sensory environment. This course will introduce  key concepts in motor control of mammalian, human  movement, coordination of movement, motor program  selection, motor program execution, motor unit  recruitment, skeletal muscle excitation-contraction coupling. This course is required for students wishing to gain certification by the Ontario Kinesiology Association.
HK*3100.Restriction: Restricted to BSCH.HK and NEUR majors/minors.
HK*3100.Department: Department of Human Health  and Nutritional Sciences
HK*3100.Requisites:
1 of BIOM*3200, HK*3810, ZOO*3600
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HK*3401.Title: HK*3401 Human Anatomy: Dissection (0.75 Credits)
HK*3401.Description: First part of the two-semester course HK*3401/2.  A two-semester lecture and laboratory course in  human anatomy which includes a detailed study of  the skeleton, upper and lower limbs, thorax,  abdomen, pelvis, perineum, head, neck and central  nervous system. The labs involve hands-on  dissection. This is a two-semester course offered  over consecutive semesters. When you select it  you must select HK*3401 in the Fall semester and  HK*3402 in the Winter semester. A grade will not  be assigned to HK*3401 until HK*3402 has been  completed.
HK*3401.Restriction: HK*3401, HK*3402  Registration in the BSC. Major in Human Kinetics  or Bio-Medical Science. Instructor consent  required.
HK*3401.Department: Department of Human  Health and Nutritional Sciences
HK*3401.Requisites: BIOM*3200 or HK*3810   - Must be taken either prior to or at the same time as this course.

HK*3402.Title: HK*3402 Human Anatomy: Dissection (0.75 Credits)
HK*3402.Description: Second part of the two-semester course HK*3401/2.  A two-semester lecture and laboratory course in  human anatomy which includes a detailed study of  the skeleton, upper and lower limbs, thorax,  abdomen, pelvis, perineum, head, neck and central  nervous system. The labs involve hands-on  dissection. This is a two-semester course offered  over consecutive semesters. When you select it  you must select HK*3401 in the Fall semester and  HK*3402 in the Winter semester. A grade will not  be assigned to HK*3401 until HK*3402 has been  completed.
HK*3402.Department: Department of Human  Health and Nutritional Sciences
HK*3402.Requisites:
HK*3401
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HK*3501.Title: HK*3501 Human Anatomy: Prosection (0.75 Credits)
HK*3501.Description: First part of the two-semester course HK*3501/2.  A two-semester lecture and laboratory course in  human anatomy which includes a detailed study of  the skeleton, upper and lower limbs, thorax,  abdomen, pelvis, perineum, head, neck and central  nervous system. Labs involve observation of  anatomical details using prosections and  dissected specimens. This is a two-semester  course offered over consecutive semesters. When  you select it you must select HK*3501 in the Fall  semester and HK*3502 in the Winter semester. A  grade will not be assigned to HK*3501 until  HK*3502 has been completed.
HK*3501.Restriction: HK*3401, HK*3402 Registration in the BSC. Major  in Human Kinetics or Bio-Medical Science.  Instructor consent required.
HK*3501.Department: Department of Human Health and Nutritional  Sciences
HK*3501.Requisites: HK*3810 OR BIOM*3200   - Must be taken either prior to or at the same time as this course.

HK*3502.Title: HK*3502 Human Anatomy: Prosection (0.75 Credits)
HK*3502.Description: Second part of the two-semester course HK*3501/2.  A two-semester lecture and laboratory course in  human anatomy which includes a detailed study of  the skeleton, upper and lower limbs, thorax,  abdomen, pelvis, perineum, head, neck and central  nervous system. Labs involve observation of  anatomical details using prosections and  dissected specimens. This is a two-semester  course offered over consecutive semesters. When  you select it you must select HK*3501 in the Fall  semester and HK*3502 in the Winter semester. A  grade will not be assigned to HK*3501 until  HK*3502 has been completed.
HK*3502.Department: Department of Human Health and Nutritional  Sciences
HK*3502.Requisites:
HK*3501
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

HK*3600.Title: HK*3600 Applied Human Kinetics I (0.75 Credits)
HK*3600.Description: This course covers laboratory techniques which  are central to human biology, together with their  underlying concepts. Human performance and  function are evaluated through cellular, organic,  systemic and whole person studies. The student's  technical competence and conceptual understanding  are emphasized.
HK*3600.Restriction: Registration in  the Human Kinetics major.
HK*3600.Department: Department of Human Health and Nutritional  Sciences
HK*3600.Requisites:
HK*2270
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
HK*3600.Locations: HK*3810   - Must be taken either prior to or at the same time as this course.

HK*3810.Title: HK*3810 Human Physiology II (0.75 Credits)
