PHYS*4540.Description: Physical methods of determining macromolecular  structure: energetics, intramolecular and  intermolecular forces, with applications to  lamellar structures, information storage, DNA and  RNA, recognition and rejection of foreign  molecules.
PHYS*4540.Requisites:
0.50 credits in biochemistry, (CHEM*3860 or PHYS*3230)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

PHYS*4910.Title: PHYS*4910 Advanced Topics in Physics I (0.5 Credits)
PHYS*4910.Description: The content of this course is determined by the  interests of the students. Possible topics  include fluid mechanics, theory of elastic  solids, general relativity, astrophysics, and  chaos. This course is not offered every year.
PHYS*4910.Requisites:
(1 of MATH*1160, MATH*2150, MATH*2160), (MATH*2170 or  MATH*2270), [(PHYS*2450, PHYS*2470) or (PHYS*2180 ,  PHYS*2310, PHYS*2340)]
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
PHYS*4910.Locations:
(1 of MATH*1160, MATH*2150, MATH*2160), (MATH*2170 or  MATH*2270), [(PHYS*2450, PHYS*2470) or (PHYS*2180 ,  PHYS*2310, PHYS*2340)]
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

PHYS*4920.Title: PHYS*4920 Advanced Topics in Physics II (0.5 Credits)
PHYS*4920.Description: The content of this course is determined by the  interests of the students. Possible topics  include fluid mechanics, theory of elastic  solids, general relativity, astrophysics, and  chaos. This course is not offered every year.
PHYS*4920.Requisites:
(1 of MATH*1160, MATH*2150, MATH*2160), (MATH*2170 or  MATH*2270), [(PHYS*2450 , PHYS*2470) or (PHYS*2180 ,  PHYS*2310, PHYS*2340)]
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
PHYS*4920.Locations:
(1 of MATH*1160, MATH*2150, MATH*2160), (MATH*2170 or  MATH*2270), [(PHYS*2450 , PHYS*2470) or (PHYS*2180 ,  PHYS*2310, PHYS*2340)]
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

PHYS*4930.Title: PHYS*4930 Advanced Topics in Physics III (0.5 Credits)
PHYS*4930.Description: The content of this course is determined by the  interests of the students. Possible topics  include fluid mechanics, theory of elastic  solids, general relativity, astrophysics, and  chaos. This course is not offered every year.
PHYS*4930.Requisites:
(1 of MATH*1160, MATH*2150, MATH*2160), (MATH*2170 or  MATH*2270), [(PHYS*2450, PHYS*2470) or (PHYS*2180 ,  PHYS*2310, PHYS*2340)]
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
PHYS*4930.Locations:
(1 of MATH*1160, MATH*2150, MATH*2160), (MATH*2170 or  MATH*2270), [(PHYS*2450, PHYS*2470) or (PHYS*2180 ,  PHYS*2310, PHYS*2340)]
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*1150.Title: POLS*1150 Understanding Politics (0.5 Credits)
POLS*1150.Description: This is the recommended introductory course for  students intending to pursue a specialization in  Political Science. An introduction to the basic  concepts of politics, such as liberty, equality,  social justice, constitutionalism, sovereignty,  federalism, parliamentary versus presidential  government. The course will emphasize the meaning  and use of these terms within Canada in the  context of other political systems.

POLS*1500.Title: POLS*1500 World Politics (0.5 Credits)
POLS*1500.Description: An examination of the fundamental patterns of  international politics, focusing especially on  the major issues and contemporary events at the  root of international conflict. As well, the  reality of globalization and interdependence is  assessed in terms of the alternative patterns of  international cooperation in the contemporary  world.
POLS*1500.Offering: Also offered through  Distance Education format.

POLS*2000.Title: POLS*2000 Political Theory (0.5 Credits)
POLS*2000.Description: A study of the philosophic and ideological  developments which have led to the emergence of  the modern state and contemporary politics.
POLS*2000.Offering: Also offered through Distance Education format.

POLS*2100.Title: POLS*2100 Comparative Politics (0.5 Credits)
POLS*2100.Description: The course provides an introduction to key concepts used in comparative political analysis.
POLS*2100.Requisites: 2.00 credits   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*2150.Title: POLS*2150 Gender and Politics (0.5 Credits)
POLS*2150.Description: This course introduces students to competing  approaches to gender and politics. Students will  examine the interrelationship of gender, politics  and the state, focusing on its implications for  political mobilization, representation and  participation, public policy, global gender  issues in international relations, and cultural  and regional differences in gender politics. The  course provides the student with the conceptual  and analytical tools for upper-year courses on  politics in general and on gender, sexuality and  politics in particular.

POLS*2200.Title: POLS*2200 International Relations (0.5 Credits)
POLS*2200.Description: An introduction to basic theories and concepts in  the study of international relations, including  an analysis of power, national interest,  security, survival, nationalism, sovereignty,  decision-making, interdependence, integration,  and transnationalism.

POLS*2230.Title: POLS*2230 Public Policy (0.5 Credits)
POLS*2230.Description: The course introduces students to public policy,  including the differences between applied and  explanatory policy analyses, within the larger  context of politics and government. Case studies  of different policy areas are used to illustrate  the challenges of developing, implementing, and  explaining policy in various (and often  interrelated) contexts from the local to the  global.
POLS*2230.Offering: Also offered through  Distance Education format.
POLS*2230.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*2250.Title: POLS*2250 Public Admin & Governance (0.5 Credits)
POLS*2250.Description: The course explores, from both practical and  theoretical perspectives, planning and  implementation of programs and services through  government departments and agencies and  "alternative" processes and structures, sometimes  involving non-governmental actors. The course  critically evaluates the changing role of  bureaucracy; financial and human resource  management; and the evolving concepts of  responsibility and accountability.
POLS*2250.Offering: Also offered through Distance Education  format.
POLS*2250.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*2300.Title: POLS*2300 Cdn Government & Politics (0.5 Credits)
POLS*2300.Description: This course explores the core institutions of  Canadian government, including parliamentary  government, federalism, the Charter of Rights and  Freedoms and electoral systems. How these  institutions shape and are shaped by political  parties and social forces, as well as current  issues like Quebec nationalism, identity politics  and Indigenous governance, are covered.
POLS*2300.Offering: Also offered through Distance  Education format.

POLS*2350.Title: POLS*2350 Law and Politics (0.5 Credits)
POLS*2350.Description: This course will consider law as both the output  of political action and as the structure in which  political action occurs. It will introduce  students to core legal concepts, explore the  impact of law on private and public actors, and  help students develop legal research skills.
POLS*2350.Requisites:
2.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*2650.Title: POLS*2650 Political Inquiry & Research (0.5 Credits)
POLS*2650.Description: This course offers an introduction to the  principles of inquiry in political science.  Students will study the crucial components of  research and engage subjects such as  theorization, research ethics, conceptualization,  operationalization, research design, case  selection, and both quantitative and qualitative  methods of data collection.
POLS*2650.Requisites: 4.00 credits including (1 of IDEV*1000, JLS*1000, POLS*1150)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3000.Title: POLS*3000 Politics of Africa (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3000.Description: Africa in the 20th Century has been the scene of  rapid political and economic change. This course  analyzes African politics in the light of  contemporary problems of development and  modernization.
POLS*3000.Requisites:
1 of IDEV*2000, POLS*2080, POLS*2100
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3020.Title: POLS*3020 Intl Law and Orgs (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3020.Description: The course explores the nature of international law and organizations and critically analyzes theories and evidence about the relationship between international law and state and non-state actors. Topics covered may include international criminal law, use of force, the environment, trade, human rights, and aid and development.
POLS*3020.Requisites: 1 of IDEV*2400, POLS*2200, POLS*2350   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3050.Title: POLS*3050 Canadian Campaigns & Elections (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3050.Description: This course provides an introduction to the  electoral process in Canada. It will explore  factors that explain citizens' vote choices and  the strategies used by candidates and their  campaigns to win these votes. The course  integrates literature on the electoral system,  campaign financing, political parties, political  communication, and voting behaviour.
POLS*3050.Requisites:
POLS*1400 or POLS*2300
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3060.Title: POLS*3060 The Middle East & North Africa (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3060.Description: Students will examine the political dynamics of  selected states and societies (e.g. Egypt, Syria,  Saudi Arabia, Iran, Israel, Jordan and Algeria)  in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA).  Issues to be covered: the impact of early Middle  Eastern/North African history upon today's  politics; class structures in the MENA countries  and their impact on politics; the rise of Arab  nationalism; Zionism; the politics of oil; the  status of women; the political impact of economic  restructuring; Islamic movements; state-building;  and political liberalization and democratization  in the Middle East and North Africa.
POLS*3060.Requisites:
1 of IDEV*2000, POLS*2080, POLS*2100
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3080.Title: POLS*3080 Politics of Latin America (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3080.Description: An exploration of Latin American politics from a  multidimensional perspective. It analyzes the  interaction among contemporary political  structures, ideologies and processes in the  context of socio-economic change.
POLS*3080.Requisites:
1 of IDEV*2000, POLS*2080, POLS*2100
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3130.Title: POLS*3130 Law, Pol & Judicial Process (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3130.Description: This course emphasizes the study of the judicial  system as a branch of government and highlights  the interaction between the judiciary, law, the  political process and public policy. Issues such  as judicial selection and Charter of Rights  decisions by courts will be explored. Comparisons  with the judicial process in other countries will  supplement the focus on the Canadian judicial  process.
POLS*3130.Requisites: 1 of POLS*2250, POLS*2300, POLS*2350   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3140.Title: POLS*3140 Charter of Rights and Freedoms (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3140.Description: This course examines the legal and political  effects of the Canadian Charter of Rights and  Freedoms. Issues to be examined may include the  Charter's influence on Canadian political culture  and identity, interest groups and social  movements, the power of the courts, and public  policy. Analysis of specific Charter sections and  judicial decisions along with comparisons to  other countries will be used to aid the analysis.
POLS*3140.Requisites:
POLS*2300 or POLS*2350
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3160.Title: POLS*3160 Global Gender Justice (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3160.Description: This course will introduce students to theories  and concepts of gender justice and women's  political empowerment in the Global South, the  Global North, and across borders. It will also  examine selected topics and cases such as  political representation, gender and culture,  religion, nationalism, gender and disability,  household authority, and reproductive rights.
POLS*3160.Requisites: 1 of IDEV*2000, POLS*2080, POLS*2100   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3210.Title: POLS*3210 The Constit & Can Federalism (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3210.Description: Canada's constitution and its federal system lie  at the heart of the ongoing crisis facing the  Canadian Confederation. This course examines the  major features of our constitutional development,  how the current system of intergovernmental  relations has evolved, and the challenges posed  by Canada's cultural diversity, pressures for  decentralisation, and the maintenance of national  sovereignty.
POLS*3210.Offering: Also offered through  Distance Education format.
POLS*3210.Requisites:
HIST*2600 or POLS*2300
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3230.Title: POLS*3230 Modern Political Thought (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3230.Description: This course explores the impact of modern science  and technology, and its impact on the western  tradition of justice from the seventeenth century  to the twentieth century. It will explore this  theme in writers such as Thomas Hobbes, Jonathan  Swift, J-J Rousseau, Edmund Burke, Friedrich  Nietzsche and George Grant. The exact selection  of thinkers will vary from year to year and  students are advised to check the course outline.
POLS*3230.Requisites: POLS*2000 or PHIL*2280   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3250.Title: POLS*3250 Public Policy: Challenges & Pr (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3250.Description: This course covers the dominant theories that  explain the origins and character of public  policy in Canada, and other countries. The focus  will be on both governmental and nongovernmental  actors.
POLS*3250.Requisites:
POLS*2230 or POLS*2250
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3270.Title: POLS*3270 Local Government in Ontario (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3270.Description: Municipal governments are major spenders of  public funds in Canada, and are also the level of  government closest to the people. In this course,  students will examine the major problems  confronting urban government in Ontario.
POLS*3270.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3300.Title: POLS*3300 Governing Criminal Justice (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3300.Description: The course provides an overview of the policy  process and outcomes of the Canadian criminal  justice system. Particular emphasis is placed on  examining, using various public policy and public  management perspectives, the practices and  interactions of governmental agencies within the  system, such as police agencies and boards,  departments of Justice, Solicitor-General,  corrections and parole agencies, courts and the  legal profession.
POLS*3300.Offering: Also offered  through Distance Education  format.
POLS*3300.Restriction: This is a Priority  Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to  particular programs or specializations or  semester levels during certain periods. Please  see the departmental website for more  information.
POLS*3300.Requisites:
1 of POLS*2350, POLS*2250, POLS*2300
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3320.Title: POLS*3320 Politics of Aid & Development (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3320.Description: This course examines the motivations and  mechanisms by which industrialized states have  designed and implemented foreign aid programs and  policy, primarily since the end of the Second  World War. Particular emphasis will be placed on  the role of multilateral, bilateral and  nongovernmental organizations in the delivery of  development assistance and humanitarian relief.
POLS*3320.Requisites: 1 of IDEV*2000, IDEV*2400, POLS*2080   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3340.Title: POLS*3340 Indigenous Politics in Canada (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3340.Description: This course provides an overview of the relationship between the Canadian state and Indigenous peoples by critically analyzing key historical and contemporary legal, political, and social developments in this evolving relationship.
POLS*3340.Offering: Also offered through Distance Education format.
POLS*3340.Requisites: 1 of ANTH*2660, HIST*2090, HIST*2600, INDG*1000, POLS*2230, POLS*2300   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3350.Title: POLS*3350 Comparative Law and Courts (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3350.Description: The course compares legal systems and judicial processes (such as judicial selection, decision-making, and accountability) across jurisdictions and explores similarities and differences in legal and judicial systems. The course critically analyzes the implications of these differences, such as in terms of judicial power, access to justice, and the protection of rights.
POLS*3350.Requisites: 1 of IDEV*2400, POLS*2100, POLS*2350   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3370.Title: POLS*3370 Enviro Politics & Governance (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3370.Description: This course examines environmental politics and  governance in Canada as well as in comparative  and international contexts. This is accomplished  by surveying how various political, legal,  administrative, and private-public actors and  processes influence the development and  implementation of environmental policy.
POLS*3370.Offering: Also offered through Distance  Education format.
POLS*3370.Requisites:
7.50 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3410.Title: POLS*3410 US Politics and Government (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3410.Description: This course involves a treatment of the basic  principles and institutions of national  government and politics in the United States as  well as the making and execution of public policy  at the national and state levels.
POLS*3410.Requisites:
POLS*2100 or POLS*2300
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3440.Title: POLS*3440 Corrupt. Scandal & Pol. Ethics (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3440.Description: This course will introduce students to the  phenomenon of political corruption and the study  of its incidence. Attention will be paid to  historical examples, contemporary scandals, and  analytical articles, dealing with the nature,  causes and effects, and proposed cures of  political corruption, and the ethical dilemmas  inherent in political life.
POLS*3440.Offering: Also  offered through Distance Education  format.
POLS*3440.Requisites:
5.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3450.Title: POLS*3450 European Govern & Politics (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3450.Description: Europe has forged a new form of political  organization, the European Union, in addition to  its variety of national democratic forms. This  course offers a comparative examination of  selected national governments, as well as an  exploration of this new supra-national  organization.
POLS*3450.Requisites:
4.00 credits including 1 of EURO*1050, POLS*2100, POLS*2200
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3470.Title: POLS*3470 Bus/Gov't Relations in Canada (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3470.Description: The public and private sectors in Canada have  become more and more interrelated in recent years  as evidenced by tax and expenditure policies, the  role of regulation and public enterprise, and the  increasing emphasis on consultation and  co-ordination. This course examines the evolving  relationship between governments and the private  sector in Canada, including business (both large  and small), organized labour, specific sectors  such as agriculture and consumer affairs and  voluntary organizations.
POLS*3470.Requisites: 1 of POLS*1400, POLS*2230, POLS*2250   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3490.Title: POLS*3490 Conflict & Conflict Resolution (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3490.Description: This course will examine the growing body of  literature which considers violent conflict and  its management. Materials are organized to  reflect the trajectory of many contemporary  conflicts: from explanations for violence, to  identifying conditions and means to resolve  conflict and, finally, to post-conflict  governance.
POLS*3490.Restriction: This is a Priority  Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to  particular programs or specializations or  semester levels during certain periods. Please  see the departmental website for more  information.
POLS*3490.Requisites:
1 of POLS*1500, POLS*2100, POLS*2200
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3650.Title: POLS*3650 Quantitative Methods (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3650.Description: This course examines quantitative research  methods of data analysis used in political  science. Students learn how to apply basic  descriptive and inferential statistical  procedures to research political problems and  test hypotheses. In lab, students will acquire  the skills to perform data analysis
POLS*3650.Restriction: Registration in Criminal Justice  & Public Policy or Political Science (major,  minor or area of concentration) or International  Development (major only).
POLS*3650.Requisites:
1 of POLS*2650, POLS*3180, SOAN*2120
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3670.Title: POLS*3670 Comparative Public Policy (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3670.Description: This course examines the political factors that  shape the policymaking process. Using the major  theoretical perspectives, the course compares  public policies in different countries.  Empirically, the focus is on a variety of  pressing issues that societies currently face.
POLS*3670.Requisites:
1 of POLS*2080, POLS*2100, POLS*2230
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3710.Title: POLS*3710 Gender, Sexuality & Law (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3710.Description: This course explores the relationship between sexuality, gender and sexual orientation and critically analyzes their regulation and deregulation by state and non-state actors.
POLS*3710.Requisites: 1 of PHIL*2060, POLS*2000, POLS*2150, SOAN*2400   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3790.Title: POLS*3790 Intl Political Economy (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3790.Description: This course examines major features of the  contemporary international political economy,  treating major theories and concepts within this  approach to international relations (hegemony,  globalization, interdependence, world systems  theory, etc.) and focusing on the operation of  key international institutions and regimes (i.e.  communications, trade and transport policy).
POLS*3790.Requisites: 1 of GEOG*2230, IDEV*2000, IDEV*2500, POLS*2080, POLS*2100, POLS*2200   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3850.Title: POLS*3850 Experiential Learning in Polit (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3850.Description: This course allows students to reflect upon their  involvement in some form of politically related  activity, including simulations, volunteer  programs, or internship work with government or  non-government organizations. The student must  find a faculty member from the Department of  Political Science willing to act as a supervisor  for the course. See the Political Science website  for the learning contract and other requirements  that must be completed in advance of registering  for this course.
POLS*3850.Restriction: Approval of the  experience and evaluation criteria by the  Undergraduate Committee of the Department of  Political Science. Instructor consent  required.
POLS*3850.Requisites: 10.00 credits, 2.00 of which must be in Political Science.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3890.Title: POLS*3890 Government & Politics of India (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3890.Description: The course is designed to provide a survey of the  history, society, culture, politics, government,  bureaucracy and foreign relations of India.
POLS*3890.Requisites:
1 of POLS*2080, POLS*2100, POLS*2200
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3920.Title: POLS*3920 Politics of China (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3920.Description: This course is a detailed study of the political  history of modern China and its current politics.  The main objective is to assess the extent to  which the Chinese Communist Party has fulfilled  its mandate, which is to build a sovereign and  united China as well as to modernize the country  within a socialist framework.
POLS*3920.Requisites:
1 of POLS*2080, POLS*2100, POLS*2200
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*3960.Title: POLS*3960 Sel Topics in Political Sci (0.5 Credits)
POLS*3960.Description: Readings and research in selected areas of the  discipline not covered by regular course  offerings. Students present a proposal and seek  approval from a member of the department in the  semester previous to enrolment in this course.  The method of course presentation, emphasis, and  evaluation are at the discretion of the  instructor.
POLS*3960.Requisites: 1.50 credits at the 3000 level in Political Science or equivalent   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4020.Title: POLS*4020 Global Law and Courts (1 Credits)
POLS*4020.Description: The seminar critically investigates topics in comparative, transnational, or international law and judicial processes.
POLS*4020.Restriction: POLS*4040. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
POLS*4020.Requisites: 1 of POLS*3020, POLS*3130, POLS*3350   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4030.Title: POLS*4030 Contemporary Political Theory (0.5 Credits)
POLS*4030.Description: This course provides an analysis of selected  theories and political issues discussed by  prominent 20th-Century thinkers. These  contemporary works will be examined as part of  the long tradition of political discourse dating  back to the classical period.
POLS*4030.Restriction: This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may  be restricted to particular programs or  specializations or semester levels during certain  periods. Please see the departmental website for  more information.
POLS*4030.Requisites: POLS*2000 and at least 1.00 credits at the 3000 level in  the Political Thought stream. Streams are defined under the Political Science Major.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4040.Title: POLS*4040 Adv Lec Global Law & Courts (0.5 Credits)
POLS*4040.Description: The seminar critically investigates topics in comparative, transnational, or international law and judicial processes.
POLS*4040.Restriction: POLS*4020. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
POLS*4040.Requisites: 1 of POLS*3020, POLS*3130, POLS*3350   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4050.Title: POLS*4050 Adv Topics in Law & Politics (1 Credits)
POLS*4050.Description: This course explores advanced topics in law and  politics depending on the interests of the  instructor. Potential topics include  investigating the law and politics of social  change or analyzing debates about the political  power of courts in Canada or in comparative  perspectives.
POLS*4050.Restriction: POLS*4060. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives. This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations or semester levels during certain periods. Please see the departmental website for more information.
POLS*4050.Requisites: 1 of POLS*3020, POLS*3130, POLS*3140, POLS*3350   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4060.Title: POLS*4060 Adv Lecture in Law & Politics (0.5 Credits)
POLS*4060.Description: This advanced lecture course explores topics in  law and politics. Specific topics vary depending  on the interests of the instructor. Potential  topics include the relationship between law and  social change, human rights, the relationship  between law and power, judicial decision-making,  and the relationship between law, class, gender,  race, and sexuality.
POLS*4060.Restriction: POLS*4050. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives. This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations or semester levels during certain periods. Please see the departmental website for more information.
POLS*4060.Requisites: 1 of POLS*3020, POLS*3130, POLS*3140, POLS*3350   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4070.Title: POLS*4070 Courts & Parliament (1 Credits)
POLS*4070.Description: The course critically examines the complex  relationship between the judiciary and  representative institutions. By comparing the  treatment of current political controversies  (assisted suicide, prostitution, drug treatment),  students will better appreciate the often-subtle  exchanges between the two institutions and  further enhance their research abilities in  regards to both legal and legislative processes.
POLS*4070.Restriction: This is a Priority Access Course. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations or semester levels during certain periods. Please see the departmental website for more information.
POLS*4070.Requisites:
1 of POLS*2350, POLS*3130, POLS*3300
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4090.Title: POLS*4090 Seminar in Digital Politics (1 Credits)
POLS*4090.Description: This seminar provides an analysis of the use of the internet and social media in politics.  It explores the ways in which digital technologies are changing politics, both theoretically and in current practice, and examines how individuals and institutions in Canada and internationally employ digital technologies as a part of political practice.
POLS*4090.Requisites: 12.50 credits including 5.00 credits in Political Science   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4100.Title: POLS*4100 Women, Justice & Public Policy (1 Credits)
POLS*4100.Description: This course will use gender-based analysis in  examining a series of justice and public policy  issues affecting the lives of women, including  equality rights, pay and employment equity,  domestic violence, sexual assault, family policy,  health care policy, and pornography. How do  current policies that developed out of  neoliberalism influence the lives of women in  different ways than men? How can/should they be  changed to recognize the different life  experiences of women as distinguished from men?  The primary focus of the topics covered in this  course will be Canadian.
POLS*4100.Restriction: POLS*4310. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives. This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations or semester levels during certain periods. Please see the departmental website for more information.
POLS*4100.Requisites: (2 of POLS*2150, POLS*2230, POLS*2250, POLS*2300, POLS*2350, POLS*3250) and 1.00 credits in the Public Policy, Governance and Law or Canadian Politics stream. Streams are defined under the Political Science Major.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4110.Title: POLS*4110 Crim Just Policy & Law (1 Credits)
POLS*4110.Description: The seminar critically investigates topics in criminal justice and public policy.
POLS*4110.Restriction: POLS*4130. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
POLS*4110.Requisites: 12.50 credits including POLS*3300   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4130.Title: POLS*4130 Adv Lec Crim Just Policy & Law (0.5 Credits)
POLS*4130.Description: The course critically investigates topics in criminal justice and public policy.
POLS*4130.Restriction: POLS*4110. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
POLS*4130.Requisites: 12.50 credits including POLS*3300   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4140.Title: POLS*4140 Conceptions of Canada (1 Credits)
POLS*4140.Description: This course will explore evolving conceptions of  Canadian identity and nationalism through  consideration of political culture, institutions  and constitutional arrangements. Possible topics  include: multiculturalism, Indigenous identity  and community, Quebec nationalism, social  citizenship, rights and representation, as well  as Canada's global role and significance.
POLS*4140.Restriction: This is a Priority Access  Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular  programs or specializations or semester levels  during certain periods. Please see the  departmental website for more  information.
POLS*4140.Requisites: POLS*2300 and 1.00 credits at the 3000 level in the  Canadian Politics stream. Streams are defined under the Political Science Major.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4150.Title: POLS*4150 Adv. Lect Conceptions of Can (0.5 Credits)
POLS*4150.Description: This advanced lecture course will explore  evolving conceptions of Canadian identity and  nationalism through a consideration of political  culture, institutions, and constitutional  arrangements. Possible topics include:  multiculturalism, Indigenous identity and  community, Quebec nationalism, social  citizenship, rights and representation, as well  as Canada's global role and significance.
POLS*4150.Restriction: This is a Priority Access  Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular  programs or specializations or semester levels  during certain periods. Please see the  departmental website for more information.  Students may not receive credit for both  POLS*4140 and POLS*4150
POLS*4150.Requisites:
POLS*2300, (2 of HIST*3160, POLS*3050, POLS*3210,  POLS*3270, POLS*3470)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4160.Title: POLS*4160 Multi-level Governance/Canada (1 Credits)
POLS*4160.Description: This course considers the evolving relationship  among levels of government in Canada. The growth  of cities, the growth of policy responsibilities  of provinces, the influence of international  organizations, and the development of First  Nations government in Canada all challenge the  conventional study of federal-provincial  relations in Canada. From year to year, this  course examines one or several of these  contemporary dynamics.
POLS*4160.Restriction: CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives. This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations or semester levels during certain periods. Please see the departmental website for more information.
POLS*4160.Requisites: POLS*2300 and 1.00 credits at the 3000 level in the  Canadian Politics stream. Streams are defined under the Political Science Major.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4170.Title: POLS*4170 Global Environmental Politics (1 Credits)
POLS*4170.Description: This seminar critically explores the politics of global environmental governance including the role of state and non-state actors.
POLS*4170.Requisites: 12.50 credits including POLS*3370   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4200.Title: POLS*4200 Intn'l Political Economy (1 Credits)
POLS*4200.Description: The course relies on theoretical approaches in  IPE to examine relationships between politics and  economics across national and regional levels.  The evolution of the global political economy and  its governance structures is explored, as well as  contemporary debates about globalization and  state and non-state actors' responses.  Issue-areas may include: money and power,  technology, trade, development and the  environment.
POLS*4200.Restriction: This is a Priority  Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to  particular programs or specializations or  semester levels during certain periods. Please  see the departmental website for more  information.
POLS*4200.Requisites: (1 of POLS*2080, POLS*2100, POLS*2200); and at least 1.00  credits at the 3000 level in the International Relations  and Global Studies stream. Streams are defined under the Political Science Major.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4250.Title: POLS*4250 Topics in Public Management (1 Credits)
POLS*4250.Description: This course will examine various topics related  to governance, such as public management reform,  public sector leadership, third sector  organizations or budgeting and human resources.
POLS*4250.Restriction: POLS*4270. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives. This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations or semester levels during certain periods. Please see the departmental website for more information.
POLS*4250.Requisites: POLS*2250 and 1.00 credits at the 3000 level in the Public  Policy, Governance and Law stream or the Canadian Politics  stream. Streams are defined under the Political Science Major.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4260.Title: POLS*4260 Topics in Public Policy (1 Credits)
POLS*4260.Description: This course will examine various public policy  issues such as social policy or health care  policy in a Canadian or comparative context.
POLS*4260.Restriction: POLS*4280. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives. This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations or semester levels during certain periods. Please see the departmental website for more information.
POLS*4260.Requisites: (2 of POLS*2230, POLS*2250, POLS*2300), 1.00 credits in the Public Policy, Governance and Law stream or the Canadian Politics stream.  Streams are defined under the Political Science Major.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4270.Title: POLS*4270 Adv Lect in Public Management (0.5 Credits)
POLS*4270.Description: This advanced lecture course examines various  topics related to governance, such as public  management reform, public sector leadership,  third sector organizations, or budgeting and  human resources.
POLS*4270.Restriction: POLS*4250. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives. This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations or semester levels during certain periods. Please see the departmental website for more information.
POLS*4270.Requisites: POLS*2250, and 1.00 credits at the 3000 level in the Public Policy, Governance and Law stream or the Canadian Politics stream. Streams are defined under the Political Science Major.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4280.Title: POLS*4280 Adv. Lect Public Policy (0.5 Credits)
POLS*4280.Description: The advanced lecture course will examine various  public policy issues, such as social policy,  health care policy, evnironmental policy, or  economic policy in a Canadian or comparative  context.
POLS*4280.Restriction: POLS*4260. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives. This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations or semester levels during certain periods. Please see the departmental website for more information.
POLS*4280.Requisites: (2 of POLS*2230, POLS*2250, POLS*2300), 1.00 credits in the Public Policy, Governance and Law stream or the Canadian Politics stream. Streams are defined under the Political Science Major.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4300.Title: POLS*4300 Human Rights, Ethics & Dvlpmt (1 Credits)
POLS*4300.Description: This course will examine the political and  ethical consequences of adopting a human rights  framework in national and international contexts  by both state and non-state actors. This subject  will be explored from a range of historical,  theoretical and practical perspectives.
POLS*4300.Restriction: POLS*4320. This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations or semester levels during certain periods. Please see the  departmental website for more information.
POLS*4300.Requisites: (1 of IDEV*2000, IDEV*2400, POLS*2080, POLS*2100, POLS*2200), 1.00 credits at the 3000 level in Political Science.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4310.Title: POLS*4310 Adv Lect Women, Just & Pub Pol (0.5 Credits)
POLS*4310.Description: This advanced lecture course will use  gender-based analysis in examining a series of  justice and public policy issues affecting the  lives of women, including equality rights, pay  and employment equity, domestic violence, sexual  assault, family policy, health care policy and  pornography. The primary focus of the topics  covered in the course will be Canadian, although  the experiences of women in other countries will  be covered, particularly as it relates to "best  practices" where appropriate.
POLS*4310.Restriction: POLS*4100. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives. This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations or semester levels during certain periods. Please see the departmental website for more information.
POLS*4310.Requisites: (2 of POLS*2150, POLS*2230, POLS*2250, POLS*2300, POLS*2350), and 1.00 credits in the Public Policy, Governance and Law or Canadian Politics streams. Streams are defined under the Political Science Major.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4320.Title: POLS*4320 Adv Lect Human Rights & Devel (0.5 Credits)
POLS*4320.Description: This advanced lecture course examines the  political and ethical consequences of adopting a  human rights framework in national and  international contexts by both state and  non-state actors. This subject will be explored  from a range of historical, theoretical and  practical perspectives.
POLS*4320.Restriction: POLS*4300. This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations or semester levels during certain periods. Please see the departmental website for more information.
POLS*4320.Requisites: (1 of IDEV*2000, IDEV*2400, POLS*2080, POLS*2100, POLS*2200), 1.00 credits at the 3000 level in Political Science.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4340.Title: POLS*4340 Nationalism (1 Credits)
POLS*4340.Description: The course examines the role of nationalism in  contemporary politics. Nationalism as such is  understood as a major political force in  state-building. Its impact on both global and  national politics is assessed in relation to  other forms of identity-based politics.
POLS*4340.Requisites: (1 of POLS*2000, POLS*2100, POLS*2200), 0.50 credits at  the 3000 level in the Comparative Politics stream or 0.50  credits at the 3000 level in the International Relations  and Global Studies stream. Streams are defined under the Political Science Major.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4710.Title: POLS*4710 Topics in Comparative Politics (1 Credits)
POLS*4710.Description: This course considers theories and problems in  comparative politics and government in developing  and industrialized countries. The geographical  and theoretical focus of the course will reflect  the interests of the instructor.
POLS*4710.Restriction: POLS*4760. This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations or semester levels during certain periods. Please see the departmental website for more information.
POLS*4710.Requisites: (1 of IDEV*2000, POLS*2080 or POLS*2100) and 1.00 credits at the 3000 level in the Comparative Politics stream. Streams are defined under the Political Science Major.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4720.Title: POLS*4720 Topics in Intern'l Relations (1 Credits)
POLS*4720.Description: This course considers theories and problems in  the field of International Relations. The  theoretical and/or geographical focus of the  course will reflect the interests of the  instructor.
POLS*4720.Restriction: This is a Priority  Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to  particular programs or specializations or  semester levels during certain periods. Please  see the departmental website for more  information.
POLS*4720.Requisites: POLS*2200 and 1.00 credits at the 3000 level in the  International Relations and Global Studies stream. Streams are defined under the Political Science Major.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4730.Title: POLS*4730 Int Relations of Middle East (1 Credits)
POLS*4730.Description: This course is designed as an advanced  introduction to the international relations of  the Middle East. The course focuses on theories  of international relations and their  applicability to specific case studies of Middle  Eastern politics. The course provides a critical  examination of conflicts in the region, and  contextualizes those conflicts within both  realist and neo-realist theories of international  relations. The course also provides a critical  examination of the Arab-Israeli crisis, with a  focus on peace negotiations. The course is  offered as a seminar, with a heavy emphasis on  class participation. Students participate in a  simulation of an Arab-Israeli peace negotiation.
POLS*4730.Requisites: POLS*2200 and 1.00 credit at the 3000 level in the  Comparative Politics and/or International Relations and  Global Studies streams. Streams are defined under the Political Science Major.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4740.Title: POLS*4740 Adv Topics: Rights & Liberties (1 Credits)
POLS*4740.Description: The course explores rights and liberties from  various perspectives depending on the interests  of the instructor. Potential topics include  exploring the political, social, and legal  factors and theories that explain the development  of rights and liberties; rights and liberties in  a comparative and international context; or the  philosophical and policy debates surrounding  rights and liberties.
POLS*4740.Restriction: POLS*4780. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives. This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations or semester levels during certain periods. Please see the departmental website for more information.
POLS*4740.Requisites: 2 of POLS*3020, POLS*3130, POLS*3140, POLS*3210, POLS*3300, POLS*3350.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4760.Title: POLS*4760 Adv Lecture in Compar Politics (0.5 Credits)
POLS*4760.Description: This advanced lecture course examines theories  and problems in comparative politics and  government ind developing and industrialized  countries. The geographical and theoretical focus  of the course will vary depending on the  interests of the instructor.
POLS*4760.Restriction: POLS*4710. This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations or semester levels during certain periods. Please see the departmental website for more information.
POLS*4760.Requisites: (1 of IDEV*2000, POLS*2080 or POLS*2100), 1.00 credits in the Comparative Politics stream. Streams are defined under the Political Science Major.   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

Potential topics  include exploring the political, social, and  legal factors and theories that explain the  development of rights and liberties; rights and  liberties in a comparative and international  context; or the philosophical and policy debates  surrounding rights and liberties.

POLS*4900.Title: POLS*4900 Seminar in Political Science (1 Credits)
POLS*4900.Description: This seminar-based course explores a current  issue in Political Science. Topics will vary from  year to year and will reflect the research and  teaching interests of the faculty member  directing the course. Information on the topic of  the current offering can be found on the  departmental website.

14.00 credits, including 1.00 credits in Political Science  at the 3000 level.
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4910.Title: POLS*4910 Sel Topics in Political Sci (0.5 Credits)
POLS*4910.Description: This course provides for independent reading and  research in selected areas of the discipline not  covered by regular course offerings. Prior to  enrollment in the course, approval must be  obtained from a member of the department willing  to supervise the research. Students should  approach potential supervisors with a proposal  for readings and research, which may include  reflection and expansion on a subject matter  addressed in previous course assignments.
POLS*4910.Requisites:
1.50 credits at the 3000 level in Political Science or  equivalent
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4930.Description: This course provides for independent reading and  research in selected areas of the discipline not  covered by regular course offerings. Prior to  enrollment in the course, approval must be  obtained from a member of the department willing  to supervise the research. Students should  approach potential supervisors with a proposal  for readings and research, which may include  reflection and expansion on a subject matter  addressed in previous course assignments.

   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4970.Title: POLS*4970 Hons. Poli. Sci. Research I (0.5 Credits)
POLS*4970.Description: This is Part I of the Honours Essay. Students  complete the necessary reading and research for  their Honours Essay under the supervision of a  department advisor. A research proposal is  expected by the end of the semester. Political  science majors who wish to pursue an honours  thesis must register in this course in their 7th  semester. Student selection of an approved  subject area and instructor must be completed in  the semester previous to enrolment in this  course.
POLS*4970.Restriction: Instructor consent required. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
POLS*4970.Requisites:
70% average in all POLS courses. Recommendation: Students  with less than a 75% average are advised not to take this  course.
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

POLS*4980.Title: POLS*4980 Hons. Poli. Sci. Research II (0.5 Credits)
POLS*4980.Description: This is Part II of the Honours Essay. Students  organize and write their essays under the  supervision of their advisor. Major honours  political science students must register in this  course in their 8th semester.
POLS*4980.Restriction: Instructor consent required. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
