SART*2700.Title: SART*2700 Digital Media I (0.5 Credits)
SART*2700.Description: This course provides an in-depth introduction to  the image making possibilities in digital media.  Students will learn various methods of drawing  vector-based imagery and compositing raster  images in industry-leading drawing and image  creation applications. Readings covering relevant  principles and theories in digital media will  form a critical supplement to the course. Some  computer experience is recommended.
SART*2700.Restriction: This is a Priority Access  Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular  programs, specializations, majors or semester  levels during certain periods. Please see the  department for more information.
SART*2700.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*2700.Requisites:
(1 of ARTH*1220, ARTH*1510, ARTH*1520, ARTH*2220),  SART*1050, SART*1060
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
SART*2700.Locations: SART*1060 can be taken as co-requisite   - Must be taken either prior to or at the same time as this course.

SART*2710.Title: SART*2710 Digital Media II (0.5 Credits)
SART*2710.Description: This course adds to the important key concepts  and methods unique to digital media introduced in  Digital Media I with an in-depth introduction to  animation in digital media. Students will learn a  number of basic principles and methods in  animation using industry standard digital tools.  Students will apply their understanding of these  concepts and methods for the production of a  number of short animated sequences using industry  leading vector-based animation and motion  graphics application software. Readings covering  relevant principles and theories will form a  critical supplement to the course.
SART*2710.Restriction: This is a Priority Access  Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular  programs, specializations, majors or semester  levels during certain periods. Please see the  department for more information.
SART*2710.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*2710.Requisites: SART*2700   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*2800.Title: SART*2800 Experimental Studio I (0.5 Credits)
SART*2800.Description: This course introduces students to different  processes used by the contemporary studio artist,  with an emphasis on time-based and  interdisciplinary forms of production. Students  will be actively engaged in exploring a variety  of skills, processes and concepts, in the  development of video and audio art, artist  multiples, and site-specific interventions. An  understanding of the technical, theoretical, and  historical concerns of experimental art practices  will provide a solid base for upper level  courses, where students will develop a stronger  capacity to work with media that are appropriate  to realize their ideas.
SART*2800.Restriction: This is  a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be  restricted to particular programs,  specializations, majors or semester levels during  certain periods. Please see the department for  more information.
SART*2800.Department: School of Fine  Art and Music
SART*2800.Requisites:
(1 of ARTH*1220, ARTH*1510, ARTH*1520, ARTH*2220),  SART*1050, SART*1060
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.
SART*2800.Locations: SART*1050 can be taken as co-requisite   - Must be taken either prior to or at the same time as this course.

SART*3090.Title: SART*3090 Drawing II (0.5 Credits)
SART*3090.Description: This course attempts to foster understanding of  the basis and technical issues necessary to the  making of drawings while introducing the  philosophical and critical issues related to the  discipline. This course will consider drawing as  an activity with a wide range of applications.
SART*3090.Restriction: Registration is limited to  students registered in the Art History or Studio  Art specializations with an average of 70% in all  ARTH and SART course attempts.
SART*3090.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*3090.Requisites:
SART*2090
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*3200.Title: SART*3200 Painting II (0.5 Credits)
SART*3200.Description: In this course, technical, aesthetic and  philosophical issues central to contemporary  painting will be investigated. These include  diverse approaches to representational painting  today as well as an introduction to abstraction  and other non-representational strategies.  Activities such as class discussions, field trips  and presentations on contemporary artists will  assist students to situate their own developing  practices within the field.
SART*3200.Restriction: Registration is limited to students registered in  the Art History or Studio Art specializations  with an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART  course attempts.
SART*3200.Department: School of Fine  Art and Music
SART*3200.Requisites:
SART*2200
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*3300.Title: SART*3300 Sculpture II (0.5 Credits)
SART*3300.Description: This is a technical and experimental course in which critical issues in post-modernist and contemporary sculpture will be explored and deployed. Projects will focus on skills training in the wood shop, metal shop and technologies for digital fabrication. Readings will provide an overview of post-modernist and contemporary sculpture.
SART*3300.Restriction: Registration is  limited to students registered in the Art History  or Studio Art specializations with an average of  70% in all ARTH and SART course  attempts.
SART*3300.Department: School of Fine Art and  Music
SART*3300.Requisites:
SART*2300
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*3470.Title: SART*3470 Printmaking Photo/Digital (0.5 Credits)
SART*3470.Description: This course will introduce the use of  contemporary digital imaging for printmaking  applications in etching, silkscreen and  lithography. File preparation, film input,  digital prints and mixed media approaches will be  covered. Conceptual issues will be examined in  relation to the creation of prints with  discussions around the use of digital files and  output as a source for printmaking.
SART*3470.Restriction: Registration is limited to  students registered in the Art History or Studio  Art specializations with an average of 70% in all  ARTH and SART course attempts.
SART*3470.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*3470.Requisites: SART*2460 or SART*2610   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*3480.Title: SART*3480 Digital Media III (0.5 Credits)
SART*3480.Description: This course introduces students to key methods  behind the design, development, and delivery of a  modern website. Students will gain a stronger  grasp of the syntax, standards and methods for  using HTML, CSS, and will be introduced to  JavaScript to display a variety of static and  dynamic content on the Web introduced in Digital  Media I and II. Readings covering relevant  principles and theories will give students a  stronger critical awareness of the Internet as a  medium for expression, and a variety of in-class  exercises will guide students towards the  completion of a fully functional final website.
SART*3480.Restriction: Registration is limited to  students registered in the Art History or Studio  Art specializations with an average of 70% in all  ARTH and SART course attempts.
SART*3480.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*3480.Requisites:
SART*2710
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*3600.Title: SART*3600 Digital & Non-Silver Photo (0.5 Credits)
SART*3600.Description: This course combines analogue and digital photographic technologies to connect with the medium's history and materiality. Course content will include medium or large format film photography, darkroom techniques, and an exploration of scale in digital production. Discussions, readings, and seminars will provide students with a critical and historical understanding of the art-making process.
SART*3600.Restriction: Registration is limited to students registered in the Art History or Studio Art specializations with an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART course attempts.
SART*3600.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*3600.Requisites: SART*2460 or SART*2610   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*3660.Title: SART*3660 Printmaking II (0.5 Credits)
SART*3660.Description: This course provides an introduction to stone  lithography and will continue to investigate the  formal and technical aspects of printmaking  techniques covered in SART*2460. Students will be  actively engaged in exploring contemporary  concerns in printmaking through ideas of  dissemination, sequence and systems through  scrutiny of printmaking objects and readings.
SART*3660.Department: School  of Fine Art and Music
SART*3660.Requisites:
SART*2460
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*3750.Title: SART*3750 Photography II (0.5 Credits)
SART*3750.Description: This course encourages students to develop an experimental, ambitious, and exploratory studio arts practice. Course material is presented through lectures, labs, and critiques to engage with the form, content, and technical attributes of the medium. Students will explore the creative uses of colour and scale. In-class discussions, readings and seminars are designed to provide students with a critical and historical understanding of the art-making process.
SART*3750.Restriction: Registration is limited to students registered in the Art History or Studio Art specializations with an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART course attempts.
SART*3750.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*3750.Requisites:
SART*2610
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*3770.Title: SART*3770 Experimental Studio II (0.5 Credits)
SART*3770.Description: Students will explore and consider the found  object and appropriation in art, the use of  language and text in art, and other conceptual  art practices in various media. In a context of  critical reading, writing, class exercises and  discussion - students will continue developing  their technical skills in video and sound  production. We may also consider such forms as  collage, the artist book and/or artist multiple,  performance, social practice art, and other  experimental studio strategies.
SART*3770.Restriction: Registration is limited to students registered in  the Art History or Studio Art specializations  with an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART  course attempts.
SART*3770.Department: School of Fine  Art and Music
SART*3770.Requisites:
SART*2800
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*3800.Title: SART*3800 Experiential Learning I (0.5 Credits)
SART*3800.Description: This is an independent study course based on  Studio Art-related practical experience.  Evaluation will be based on assignments related  to work duties. Written proposals, signed by the  supervisor and a faculty member, must be  submitted to the Director for the School for  approval by the last day of course selection in  the Fall (for Winter) or Winter (for the  following Summer or Fall).
SART*3800.Restriction: Registration is limited to students registered in  the Art History or Studio Art specializations  with an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART  course attempts. Instructor consent  required.
SART*3800.Department: School of Fine Art and  Music
SART*3800.Requisites:
3.00 credits in Studio Art
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*3900.Title: SART*3900 Experiential Learning II (0.5 Credits)
SART*3900.Description: This course provides students with an opportunity  to continue the workplace or activity begun in  SART*3800 in greater depth, or to experience a  new work/study situation. Evaluation will be  based on assignments related to work duties.  Written proposals, signed by the supervisor and a  faculty member, must be submitted to the Director  for the School for approval by the last day of  course selection in the Fall (for Winter) or  Winter (for the following Summer or Fall)  semester.
SART*3900.Restriction: Registration is  limited to students registered in the Art History  or Studio Art specializations with an average of  80% in all ARTH and SART course attempts.  Instructor consent required.
SART*3900.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*3900.Requisites:
SART*3800 and 3.50 credits in Studio Art
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4090.Title: SART*4090 Drawing III (0.5 Credits)
SART*4090.Description: This course will study the technical development  of observational drawing as well as the  experimental and intentional development of  drawing as a contemporary art form. Drawings will  be made and discussed with attention to semiotic  theory in order to examine the production and  interpretation of meaning.
SART*4090.Restriction: Registration is limited to students registered in  the Studio Art Major with an average of 70% in  all ARTH and SART course attempts. This is a  Priority Access Course. Some restrictions may  apply during some time periods.
SART*4090.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*4090.Requisites:
SART*3090
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4130.Title: SART*4130 Drawing IV (1 Credits)
SART*4130.Description: This is an advanced course which explores drawing  through individually oriented production  supported by critical study of diverse  contemporary approaches to the medium. In this  course drawings will continue to be considered in  the light of semiotic theory in order to examine  the production and interpretation of meaning.
SART*4130.Restriction: Registration is limited to  students registered in the Studio Art Major with  an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART course  attempts. This is a Priority Access Course. Some  restrictions may apply during some time  periods.
SART*4130.Department: School of Fine Art and  Music
SART*4130.Requisites:
SART*4090
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4200.Title: SART*4200 Painting III (0.5 Credits)
SART*4200.Description: This course focuses on experimentation as a means  to investigate the possibilities available to a  contemporary painter. Representational and  non-representational approaches will continue to  be explored, with emphasis on the development of  the student's own research interests. Critical  readings, in-class discussions and gallery visits  help position their research within the  discourse. Paintings will be analyzed with  attention to semiotic theory in order to examine  the production and interpretation of meaning.
SART*4200.Restriction: Registration is limited to  students registered in the Studio Art Major with  an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART course  attempts. This is a Priority Access Course. Some  restrictions may apply during some time  periods.
SART*4200.Department: School of Fine Art and  Music
SART*4200.Requisites: SART*3200   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4240.Title: SART*4240 Painting IV (1 Credits)
SART*4240.Description: This capstone course offers advanced  investigations into the theory and practice of  painting, with strong emphasis on the development  of a critically informed and engaged individual  painting practice. Studio work is supplemented  with critical readings and a gallery field trip.  Students collaborate to mount an exhibition of  their work at the end of the semester.
SART*4240.Restriction: Registration is limited to  students registered in the Studio Art Major with  an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART course  attempts. This is a Priority Access Course. Some  restrictions may apply during some time  periods.
SART*4240.Department: School of Fine Art and  Music
SART*4240.Requisites:
SART*4200
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4250.Title: SART*4250 Topics in Painting & Drawing (0.5 Credits)
SART*4250.Description: This is a variable-content advanced course where  topics change every year and each allows for  in-depth focus on a specific theme, subject or  technique of interest to both painting and  drawing students. Studio work will be supported  by readings in contemporary theory and criticism  and lectures on pertinent artists. The emphasis  is on contemporary approaches to artmaking.
SART*4250.Restriction: Registration is limited to  students registered in the Art History  specialization or Studio Art Major. with an  average of 70% in all ARTH and SART course  attempts. This is a Priority Access Course. Some  restrictions may apply during some time  periods.
SART*4250.Department: School of Fine Art and  Music
SART*4250.Requisites:
SART*3090 or SART*3200
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4260.Title: SART*4260 Topics in Painting & Drawing (0.5 Credits)
SART*4260.Description: This is a variable-content advanced course where  topics change every year and each allows for  in-depth focus on a specific theme, subject or  technique of interest to both painting and  drawing students. Studio work will be supported  by readings in contemporary theory and criticism  and lectures on pertinent artists. The emphasis  is on contemporary approaches to artmaking.
SART*4260.Restriction: Registration is limited to  students registered in the Art History  specialization or Studio Art Major. with an  average of 70% in all ARTH and SART course  attempts. This is a Priority Access Course. Some  restrictions may apply during some time  periods.
SART*4260.Department: School of Fine Art and  Music
SART*4260.Requisites:
SART*3090 or SART*3200
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4300.Title: SART*4300 Sculpture III (0.5 Credits)
SART*4300.Description: Contemporary sculpture will be explored through studio projects, readings, and critiques. In close consultation with the instructor, students will pursue at least one self-directed project in sculpture in an environment that emphasizes production, independent research, and group interaction. Readings will provide an overview of contemporary sculpture. Interdisciplinary projects based on the students' research are welcomed.
SART*4300.Restriction: Registration is limited to students registered in the Studio Art Major with an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART course attempts. This is a Priority Access Course. Some restrictions may apply during some time periods.
SART*4300.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*4300.Requisites:
SART*3300
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4330.Title: SART*4330 Sculpture IV (1 Credits)
SART*4330.Description: Contemporary sculpture will be explored through studio projects, readings, and critiques. In close consultation with the instructor, students will pursue at least two self-directed sculptural projects in an environment that emphasizes production, independent research, and group interaction. Interdisciplinary projects based on the students' research are welcomed.
SART*4330.Restriction: Registration is limited to students registered in the Art History or Studio Art specializations with an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART course attempts. This is a Priority Access Course. Some restrictions may apply during some time periods.
SART*4330.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*4330.Requisites:
SART*4300
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4410.Title: SART*4410 Printmaking III (0.5 Credits)
SART*4410.Description: Contemporary issues in printmaking will be  addressed through studio projects, readings and  independent work in close consultation with the  instructor. Interdisciplinary projects will be  encouraged using any of the techniques studied in  printmaking to this point. Conceptual approaches,  including prints and installation, modular and  sculptural applications can be explored.
SART*4410.Restriction: Registration is limited to  students registered in the Studio Art Major with  an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART course  attempts. This is a Priority Access Course. Some  restrictions may apply during some time  periods.
SART*4410.Department: School of Fine Art and  Music
SART*4410.Requisites: 1 of SART*3470, SART*3660, (SART*2460, SART*3600)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4470.Title: SART*4470 Printmaking IV (1 Credits)
SART*4470.Description: This course focuses on independent work with an  emphasis on an experimental use of printmaking  media. Students will continue to investigate  digital and traditional printmaking methods.  There will be greater emphasis on the critical  issues relevant to printmaking with attention to  clarity of personal statement, originality and  professionalism both in studio practice and  discussion.
SART*4470.Restriction: Registration is  limited to students registered in the Studio Art  Major with an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART  course attempts. This is a Priority Access  Course. Some restrictions may apply during some  time periods.
SART*4470.Department: School of Fine Art  and Music
SART*4470.Requisites:
SART*4410
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4660.Title: SART*4660 Topics in Experimental Studio (0.5 Credits)
SART*4660.Description: For this advanced course, a specific and timely  theme, subject, or technique will be explored in  a context of critical reading, writing, class  exercises and discussion. Topics will vary  according to the proposals of artist-instructors.  Students will be encouraged to produce works in  media such as video art, audio art, artist book  and/or multiple, performance, social practice  art, interventions, and other "post-studio" and  experimental studio practices.
SART*4660.Restriction: Registration is limited to students registered in  the Art History or Studio Art specializations  with an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART  course attempts.
SART*4660.Department: School of Fine  Art and Music
SART*4660.Requisites:
SART*3770
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4670.Title: SART*4670 Topics in Experimental Studio (0.5 Credits)
SART*4670.Description: For this advanced course, a specific and timely  theme, subject, or technique will be explored in  a context of critical reading, writing, class  exercises and discussion. Topics will vary  according to the proposals of artist-instructors.  Students will be encouraged to produce works in  media such as video art, audio art, artist book  and/or multiple, performance, social practice  art, interventions, and other "post-studio" and  experimental studio practices.
SART*4670.Restriction: Registration is limited to students registered in  the Art History or Studio Art specializations  with an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART  course attempts.
SART*4670.Department: School of Fine  Art and Music
SART*4670.Requisites:
SART*3770
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4700.Title: SART*4700 Photography III (0.5 Credits)
SART*4700.Description: This course provides students with the opportunity to generate and complete a self-directed or collaborative body of work. Students will explore various approaches to historical and contemporary modes of photography, with an emphasis on experimental, hybrid, and material-based approaches to the medium. An emphasis will be placed on conceptual development, exploring the interaction of formal and representational concerns within the practice of photography.
SART*4700.Restriction: Registration is limited to students registered in the Studio Art Major with an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART course attempts. This is a Priority Access Course. Some restrictions may apply during some time periods.
SART*4700.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*4700.Requisites: 1 of SART*3600, SART*3750, (SART*2610, SART*3470)    - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4720.Title: SART*4720 Photography IV (1 Credits)
SART*4720.Description: This course will emphasize research, problem solving, technical experimentation, and material and aesthetic project development. Students can choose to work with black and white, colour, non-silver, digital, or hybrid photographic techniques to produce a body of work. Opportunities for interdisciplinary approaches to photographic practice and independent and sustained research methodologies will be encouraged. The course will also cover professional skills, such as how to write an artist statement, how to apply for funding, and how to organize, curate and install a group exhibition or public installation.
SART*4720.Restriction: Registration is limited to students registered in the Art History or Studio Art specializations with an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART course attempts. This is a Priority Access Course. Some restrictions may apply during some time periods.
SART*4720.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*4720.Requisites:
SART*4700
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4750.Title: SART*4750 Specialized Studio Practice I (1 Credits)
SART*4750.Description: This is an advanced and specialized course in  individual studio work, which affords students  opportunities for interdisciplinary and  collaborative approaches and oversees the  development of independent study strategies.  Students will research and complete a major  self-directed project. This course is not  intended for all Honours students. This course is  intended to assist in the preparation for  graduate school and professional activities in  the Arts.
SART*4750.Restriction: Instructor consent  required. Selection is by a process of portfolio  submission and interview.
SART*4750.Department: School  of Fine Art and Music
SART*4750.Requisites:
A minimum of 0.50 credits at the 4000-level in Studio Arts,  a minimum cumulative average of at least 80% in SART  courses and ARTH courses, 6.50 credits in SART and ARTH.
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4760.Title: SART*4760 Specialized Studio Practice II (1 Credits)
SART*4760.Description: This course is a continuation of SART*4750.
SART*4760.Restriction: Instructor consent required.  Selection for entry into SART*4750 is by a  process of portfolio submission and  interview.
SART*4760.Department: School of Fine Art and  Music
SART*4760.Requisites:
SART*4750
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4800.Title: SART*4800 Special Topics in Sculpture (0.5 Credits)
SART*4800.Description: This is an advanced course which focuses on a  specific topic, concept or technique in  sculpture. Subject matter will vary according to  the instructor or instructors and will consist of  topics not otherwise available in the curriculum.  Topics may include, for example, digital media,  public art, mold making, and installation.
SART*4800.Restriction: Registration is limited to  students registered in the Art History or Studio  Art specializations with an average of 70% in all  ARTH and SART course attempts.
SART*4800.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*4800.Requisites:
SART*3300
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4810.Title: SART*4810 Experimental Studio III (0.5 Credits)
SART*4810.Description: This course will consist of thematic projects  that elaborate on issues and practices that are  timely and significant to contemporary art. In a  context of critical reading, writing, class  exercise and discussion - students will be  encouraged to consider various forms and media to  realize their ideas. Students will continue  developing their technical skills in video and  sound production and are encouraged to explore  such forms as collage, assemblage, the artist  book and/or multiple, performance, social  practice art, interventions, and other  "post-studio" and experimental studio strategies.
SART*4810.Restriction: Registration is limited to  students registered in the Studio Art Major with  an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART course  attempts. This is a Priority Access Course. Some  restrictions may apply during some time  periods.
SART*4810.Department: School of Fine Art and  Music
SART*4810.Requisites:
1 of SART*3770, SART*4660, SART*4670
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4870.Title: SART*4870 Special Topics in Sculpture (0.5 Credits)
SART*4870.Description: This is an advanced course which focuses on a  specific topic, concept or technique in  sculpture. Subject matter will vary according to  the instructor or instructors and will consist of  topics not otherwise available in the curriculum.  Topics may include, for example, digital media,  public art, mold making, and installation.
SART*4870.Restriction: Registration is limited to  students registered in the Art History or Studio  Art specializations with an average of 70% in all  ARTH and SART course attempts.
SART*4870.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*4870.Requisites:
SART*3300
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4880.Title: SART*4880 Experimental Studio IV (1 Credits)
SART*4880.Description: In this capstone course students will respond to  thematic projects that elaborate on issues and  practices that are timely and significant in  contemporary art, in addition to producing and  independent project centered on their own  research, in close consultation with the  instructor. In a context of critical reading,  writing, class exercises and discussion, students  are expected to produce professional quality  artworks in forms such as video art, audio art,  artist book and/or multiple, performance, social  practice art, interventions, and other  "post-studio" and experimental studio strategies.  Students will also develop professional skills  including giving presentations on their work,  writing artist statements and exhibition  proposals
SART*4880.Restriction: Registration is  limited to students registered in the Studio Art  Major with an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART  course attempts. This is a Priority Access  Course. Some restrictions may apply during some  time periods.
SART*4880.Department: School of Fine Art  and Music
SART*4880.Requisites:
1 of SART*4660, SART*4670, SART*4810
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4890.Title: SART*4890 Digital Media IV (1 Credits)
SART*4890.Description: This course examines the intellectual and  creative ethic of the Internet and considers the  realities of establishing an art practice in a  culture of instant gratification and overwhelming  interruptions. Informed by course readings and  self-directed research, students create  multimedia projects that engage the Internet as a  distinct contemporary medium.
SART*4890.Restriction: Registration is limited to students registered in  the Studio Art Major with an average of 70% in  all ARTH and SART course attempts. This is a  Priority Access Course. Some restrictions may  apply during some time periods.
SART*4890.Department: School of Fine Art and Music
SART*4890.Requisites:
SART*3480
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4900.Title: SART*4900 Critical Practices: Studio Art (1 Credits)
SART*4900.Description: This capstone Studio Art course is an advanced and specialized program that encourages individual studio work, interdisciplinary and collaboration, and the development of independent study strategies. Students undertake a major self-directed project, preparing them for graduate school and professional pursuits in the Arts. While primarily self-directed, weekly classes include seminars, lectures and student presentations with a focus on contemporary art.
SART*4900.Restriction: Restricted to SART majors with an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART course attempts.
SART*4900.Department: School of Fine Art and  Music
SART*4900.Requisites: 2 of SART*4090, SART*4200, SART*4300, SART*4410, SART*4700, SART*4810   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SART*4910.Title: SART*4910 Independent Studio (1 Credits)
SART*4910.Description: This capstone course emphasizes individual studio work, interdisciplinary collaboration, and independent study strategies by completing a major self-directed project. The course also includes seminars on professional skills for artists and concludes with a group exhibition organized by participants.
SART*4910.Restriction: Restricted to SART majors with an average of 70% in all ARTH and SART course attempts.
SART*4910.Department: School of Fine Art and  Music
SART*4910.Requisites: 2 of SART*4090, SART*4200, SART*4300, SART*4410, SART*4700, SART*4810   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*2111.Title: SOAN*2111 Classical Theory (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*2111.Description: First part of the two-semester course  SOAN*2111/2. This course explores the origins and  early development of sociological theory in its  classical and early contemporary traditions. When  you select it you must select SOAN*2111 in the  Fall semester and SOAN*2112 in the Winter  semester. A grade will not be assigned to  SOAN*2111 until SOAN*2112 has been completed.
SOAN*2111.Requisites:
1 of ANTH*1150, SOC*1100, SOC*1500
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*2112.Title: SOAN*2112 Classical Theory (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*2112.Description: Second part of the two-semester course  SOAN*2111/2. This course explores the origins and  early development of sociological theory in its  classical and early contemporary traditions. When  you select it you must select SOAN*2111 in the  Fall semester and SOAN*2112 in the Winter  semester. A grade will not be assigned to  SOAN*2111 until SOAN*2112 has been completed.
SOAN*2112.Requisites:
SOAN*2111
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*2120.Title: SOAN*2120 Introductory Methods (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*2120.Description: A general introduction to the process of social  research emphasizing research design, techniques  of data collection, analysis and interpretation  of research results.
SOAN*2120.Restriction: Restricted to students in ANTH, ANTH:C, BECN, CJPP, CJPP:C, IDS, IDS:C, JLS, JLS:C, BOH, BOH:C, SOC, BAG.ARTS
SOAN*2120.Requisites: 1 of ANTH*1150, IDEV*1000, SOC*1100, SOC*1500   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*2290.Title: SOAN*2290 Identities & Cultural Diver (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*2290.Description: An examination of the interrelationships among  Canadian ethnic, racial and linguistic groups  including their locations in the Canadian mosaic.
SOAN*2290.Requisites:
ANTH*1150 or SOC*1100
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*2400.Title: SOAN*2400 Introduction to Gender Systems (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*2400.Description: An introduction to the examination of the  characteristics of gender relationships both  historically and cross-culturally. Amongst the  emphases are theoretical approaches to gender  analysis, methodologies, case studies and  attention to themes such as class and  stratification, race and ethnicity, identities  and global restructuring as these shape gender  dynamics.
SOAN*2400.Offering: Also offered through  Distance Education format.
SOAN*2400.Requisites: 1 of ANTH*1150, IDEV*1000, SOC*1100   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*3040.Title: SOAN*3040 Globalization, Work & Orgs (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*3040.Description: This course examines the social, economic, and  political dimensions of work, locating work and  its transformation within the broader context of  globalization, economic restructuring, and shifts  in public policy. Theoretical approaches and  concepts used in the study of work will be  introduced and critically assessed.
SOAN*3040.Requisites: 1 of ANTH*2160, ANTH*2180, SOAN*2112   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*3070.Title: SOAN*3070 Qualitative & Observational M (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*3070.Description: Non-quantitative techniques in social research  including participant observation, unobtrusive  methods, case studies and interviewing. [Restriction(s): This is a Priority Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular programs or specializations. Please see the departmental website.
SOAN*3070.Requisites: ONEH*2000 or SOAN*2120   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*3100.Title: SOAN*3100 Gender Perspectives/Families (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*3100.Description: This course explores families and households from  a gender perspective, using insights from  sociology and anthropology.
SOAN*3100.Requisites: (1 of ANTH*2160, ANTH*2180, SOAN*2112, SOAN*2400), (POLS*2650 or SOAN*2120)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*3120.Title: SOAN*3120 Quantitative Methods (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*3120.Description: This course introduces basic descriptive and  inferential techniques used in quantitative  social research. Students will acquire the skills  needed to perform basic analyses and to read the  research literature. They will also acquire  skills in using a standard computer package to  perform data analyses. Topics include: data  organization, sample description, hypothesis  testing and measures of association.
SOAN*3120.Restriction: Restricted to students  registered in Anthropology, Criminal Justice and  Public Policy, Sociology, International  Development (GAD or RAD).
SOAN*3120.Requisites:
SOAN*2120
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*3130.Title: SOAN*3130 Protest & Collective Action (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*3130.Description: The course introduces students to the study of  social movements and contentious collective  action, looking at the motivations, tactics,  outcomes of movement participants, and how these  are theorized.
SOAN*3130.Requisites: 1 of ANTH*2160, ANTH*2180, GEOG*2030, IDEV*2000, IDEV*2300, SOAN*2112   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*3240.Title: SOAN*3240 Gender & Global Inequality I (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*3240.Description: In this course, students will develop their  ability to use a gender perspective to study  social change in the context of global  inequalities. Students will develop their  knowledge of the core concepts and theories in  Gender and Development (GAD) thinking and  practice, while exploring the development process  from a critical perspective.
SOAN*3240.Requisites: 1 of ANTH*2160, ANTH*2180, IDEV*2000, IDEV*2300, SOC*2080   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*3250.Title: SOAN*3250 Social Change in Latin America (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*3250.Description: This course provides a critical, comparative  examination of the social-structural and cultural  transformations occurring in Latin America in a  context of deepening integration with the global  north. Topics to feature prominently may include  land reform, depeasantization, out-migration,  maquiladoras, informal employment, race and  ethnic relations, religiosity and religious  identification, and social movements. The  particular sub-regional focus may vary.
SOAN*3250.Requisites: 1 of ANTH*2160, ANTH*2180, IDEV*2000, SOC*2080   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*3380.Title: SOAN*3380 Culture, Society, Nature (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*3380.Description: This course focusses on interdisciplinary  explorations of contemporary intersections of  culture, society, and nature. This includes  considerations of issues such as the production  of environmental knowledge, ethics of  human-non-human interactions, the Anthropocene,  and conservation politics.
SOAN*3380.Requisites: 1 of ANTH*2230, GEOG*2210, IDEV*2000, SOC*2280   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*3680.Title: SOAN*3680 Perspectives on Development (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*3680.Description: This course examines theories and processes  relating to international development and the  responses to these by anthropologists and/or  sociologists.
SOAN*3680.Restriction: ANTH*3680.  Registration in Anthropology, Sociology or  International Development.
SOAN*3680.Requisites: 1 of ANTH*2160, ANTH*2180, IDEV*2000, IDEV*2300, SOC*2080   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*4210.Title: SOAN*4210 Indigenous-Settler Relations (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*4210.Description: This seminar-based course is designed to provide  students with an opportunity to explore  contemporary Indigenous-Settler relations in  Canadian Society. Grounded in an exploration of  worldviews and meaningful knowledge systems  engagement, the course may explore governance,  decolonisation, re-appropriation, reconciliation,  etc. The specific content areas will vary  depending on the instructor.
SOAN*4210.Requisites: 12.50 credits including (1 of ANTH*2660, IDEV*2000, IDEV*2400, GEOG*2210, SOAN*2290), (1 of GEOG*2260, IDEV*2100, POLS*2650, IES*2010, SOAN*2120, SOAN*3070)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*4220.Title: SOAN*4220 Gender & Change/Rural Canada (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*4220.Description: This course examines socio-cultural structures  affecting historically gendered positions and  roles in rural Canada.
SOAN*4220.Requisites: 12.50 credits including (1 of ANTH*2160, ANTH*2180, IDEV*2000, IDEV*2300, SOC*2080), (1 of GEOG*2260, IDEV*2100, POLS*2650, SOAN*2120)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*4230.Title: SOAN*4230 Gender & Global Inequality II (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*4230.Description: An in-depth and critical examination of a range  of gender issues in the context of development,  this course aims to enhance students' ability to  critically analyze development theory and  practices using gender analysis. It provides  students an opportunity to deepen their  understanding of gender issues in a global  context, with the aim of further equipping them  to participate effectively in gender and  development-related research, policy-making, and  implementation.
SOAN*4230.Requisites: 12.50 credits including SOAN*3240, (1 of GEOG*2260, GEOG*3090, IDEV*2100, POLS*2650, SOAN*2120)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*4250.Title: SOAN*4250 Energy and Society (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*4250.Description: This seminar addresses the links between social  relations and various types of energy including  petroleum, other hydrocarbons, nuclear and solar  energies. Topics may include corporations,  states, international organizations and popular  movements.
SOAN*4250.Requisites: 12.50 credits including (1 of IDEV*2100, GEOG*2260, POLS*2650, SOAN*2120), (1 of ANTH*2160, ANTH*2180, IDEV*2000, IDEV*2300, SOAN*2112, SOC*2080)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*4260.Title: SOAN*4260 Migration, Inequality, Change (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*4260.Description: This seminar critically examines the complex  relationships between migration, inequality and  social change. Students will develop their  understanding of key debates in contemporary  migration, exploring relevant theory, research  and public policy. Topics may include the  migration-development nexus, the role of  migration policies in structuring inequalities,  migrant rights and resistance, and transnational  families.
SOAN*4260.Requisites: 12.50 credits including (1 of IDEV*2100, GEOG*2260, POLS*2650, SOAN*2120), (1 of ANTH*2160, ANTH*2180, IDEV*2000, IDEV*2300, SOAN*2112, SOC*2080)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOAN*4320.Title: SOAN*4320 Transition: School to Work (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*4320.Description: This applied course examines the evolving  research and models in the transitions from  school to work area. There is an evolving  literature in this area based, in part, on the  successful application of research in the  transition from high school to postsecondary  education. This 'capstone' course also considers  the practical issues involved in making such a  move, considering the knowledge, skills, and  values needed by university students to succeed  in the modern workplace (public, private, and  not-for-profit sectors) in Canada. Students will  complete an "Action Sociology/Anthropology  Project," as well as a "Skills Portfolio," and  other work related to their own transition.
SOAN*4320.Restriction: Registration in Sociology,  Anthropology or Criminal Justice & Public Policy  majors in semester 7 or 8.

SOAN*4500.Title: SOAN*4500 Community Development (0.5 Credits)
SOAN*4500.Description: An analysis of approaches to community  development defined as planned, change-directed  action undertaken by individuals, groups and  organizations. The course will include the  examination of actual community development  practices.
SOAN*4500.Requisites: (1 of ANTH*2160, ANTH*2180, ONEH*2000, SOC*2080), (1 of GEOG*2210, SOAN*2120, SOAN*3070)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*1100.Title: SOC*1100 Sociology (0.5 Credits)
SOC*1100.Description: An introductory course dealing with the basic  concepts and methods of sociology applied to  societies, groups and individuals. Students will  gain an understanding of basic social processes  such as socialization, social exchange, deviance  and conformity, social change and basic social  institutions such as the economy, the polity, the  family, religion, education.
SOC*1100.Offering: Also  offered through Distance Education  format.
SOC*1100.Offered: Summer, Fall, and Winter, All Years

SOC*1500.Title: SOC*1500 Crime and Criminal Justice (0.5 Credits)
SOC*1500.Description: This course will introduce students to the study  of crime and criminal justice. It will examine  the various criminological theories, types of  criminal behaviour, and the criminal justice  system.

SOC*2010.Title: SOC*2010 Canadian Society (0.5 Credits)
SOC*2010.Description: A description of the structure of Canadian  society with its social, political and economic  tensions.
SOC*2010.Requisites:
SOC*1100
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*2070.Title: SOC*2070 Social Deviance (0.5 Credits)
SOC*2070.Description: An introduction to some of the basic theories of  deviance and social control and their application  to selected social problems.
SOC*2070.Offering: Also  offered through Distance Education  format.
SOC*2070.Restriction: This is a Priority  Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to  particular programs or specializations. Please  see the departmental website.
SOC*2070.Requisites:
SOC*1100 or SOC*1500
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*2080.Title: SOC*2080 Rural Sociology (0.5 Credits)
SOC*2080.Description: An introduction to the structure and processes of  rural society. This course deals with diverse  topics such as agrarian movements, the rise of  the agro-industrial complex, the role of the  state in agriculture, the question of community,  and rural environmental issues. A comparative  perspective is cultivated, although the primary  emphasis is on Canadian society.
SOC*2080.Requisites:
1 of ANTH*1150, IDEV*1000, GEOG*1220, SOC*1100
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*2280.Title: SOC*2280 Society, Knowledge Sys & Env (0.5 Credits)
SOC*2280.Description: This course provides students with an introduction to the nature and dimensions of the environmental crisis by examining knowledge systems and their relationships with the environment. These foundations are intended to enable respective, respectful, reciprocal, and meaningful engagement between Indigenous and science-based knowledge systems in cross-cultural environmental stewardship/governance. Issues to be examined may include climate change and variability, nuclear energy, environmental toxins, species extinction, and population growth pressures.
SOC*2280.Offering: Also offered through Distance Education format.
SOC*2280.Requisites: 1 of ANTH*1150, GEOG*1220, IDEV*1000, INDG*1000, SOC*1100   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*2390.Title: SOC*2390 Class and Stratification (0.5 Credits)
SOC*2390.Description: An examination of the persistent bases of social  inequalities such as wealth, income, power and  prestige including class formation, class  consciousness, political activity and social  mobility.
SOC*2390.Requisites:
SOC*1100
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*2700.Title: SOC*2700 Criminological Theory (0.5 Credits)
SOC*2700.Description: This course will examine the development of  criminological theory from the late 1700s to  contemporary times.
SOC*2700.Requisites:
SOC*1500
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*2760.Title: SOC*2760 Homicide (0.5 Credits)
SOC*2760.Description: This course will review legal definitions of  homicide, statistical trends in homicide-both in  Canada and internationally-and theoretical  explanations of homicide. The course will also  examine the key criminological/ sociological  empirical research studies on the various types  of homicide, such as: femicide, familialcide,  serial and mass murder.
SOC*2760.Offering: Offered  through Distance Education format  only.
SOC*2760.Restriction: This is a Priority Access  Course. Enrolment may be restricted to particular  programs or specializations. Please see the  departmental website for more  information.
SOC*2760.Requisites:
1 of ANTH*1150, FRHD*1010, PHIL*1010, POLS*1400, PSYC*1000,  PSYC*1100, PSYC*1200, SOC*1100, SOC*1500
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*3130.Title: SOC*3130 Politics and Society (0.5 Credits)
SOC*3130.Description: An interpretation of the political process and  its relationship to other aspects of the social  structure, including such topics as political  parties, movements, factions, citizen  participation, power structures and the process  of political exchange.
SOC*3130.Requisites:
SOAN*2112, SOAN*2120
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*3310.Title: SOC*3310 Contemporary Theory (0.5 Credits)
SOC*3310.Description: This course outlines and evaluates the major  theories in use today. A central aspect of the  course is instruction in the application of these  theories.
SOC*3310.Requisites:
SOAN*2112, SOAN*2120
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*3410.Title: SOC*3410 Individual and Society (0.5 Credits)
SOC*3410.Description: This course deals with the relationship between  the individual and society through close  examination of social interaction in a variety of  settings. Students will be exposed to a range of  theories, methods and concepts from cognitive,  micro, dramaturgical, and interpretive  sociologies, and will learn to apply these to the  analysis of personal relationships, intercultural  encounters, institutional life, collective  action, and everyday life-worlds.
SOC*3410.Requisites:
SOAN*2112, SOAN*2120
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*3490.Title: SOC*3490 Law and Society (0.5 Credits)
SOC*3490.Description: This course examines the social basis of law.  Specific topics include the law as an instrument  of stability or change, and the role of law  makers, law enforcers and interpreters, including  the legal profession, the police, judges and  courts.
SOC*3490.Restriction: This is a Priority  Access Course. Enrolment may be restricted to  particular programs or specializations. Please  see the departmental website.
SOC*3490.Requisites: (SOAN*2112 or SOC*2700), (POLS*2650 or SOAN*2120)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*3710.Title: SOC*3710 Youth Justice (0.5 Credits)
SOC*3710.Description: This course examines concerns about youth crime  in Canada and elsewhere. It examines the history  of legislation to control youth crime, criminal  justice processing and practices, public  reactions and concerns about youth crime and  theoretical models used to explain youth crime.
SOC*3710.Restriction: Registration in BA.ANTH, BA.CJPP, BA.SOC (major, minor or area of concentration).
SOC*3710.Requisites:
(SOAN*2112 or SOC*2700), SOAN*2120
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*3730.Title: SOC*3730 Courts and Society (0.5 Credits)
SOC*3730.Description: This course is an introduction to the social  processes involved in the court, particularly the  criminal court. Typical concerns will be the  place of courts in society, public opinion and  confidence in courts, purposes and principles of  sentencing, sentencing reforms and disparities  (e.g., across gender and race), the role of  criminal records, juries, the roles of judges,  and alternatives to criminal courts.
SOC*3730.Restriction: Registration in BA.ANTH, BA.CJPP, BA.SOC (major, minor or area of concentration).
SOC*3730.Requisites:
(SOAN*2112 or SOC*2700), SOAN*2120
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*3740.Title: SOC*3740 Corrections and Penology (0.5 Credits)
SOC*3740.Description: This course will examine the current state of  knowledge regarding the role of corrections and  penology. It will examine such specific issues as  public perception and reaction to the criminal  justice system's methods of punishment and  treatment of criminal offenders, the  effectiveness of sentencing options and policies,  including fines, probation, prison sentences and  parole. It will also examine the various  theoretical and methodological approaches to the  study of courts, corrections and penology.
SOC*3740.Restriction: Registration in BA.ANTH, BA.CJPP, BA.SOC (major, minor or area of concentration).
SOC*3740.Requisites:
(SOAN*2112 or SOC*2700), SOAN*2120
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*3750.Title: SOC*3750 Police in Society (0.5 Credits)
SOC*3750.Description: This course will examine the role of police in  society. It will examine theories of policing,  the history of policing and such issues as police  citizen interaction, relations with visible  minorities, methods for controlling police  behaviour, and the effectiveness of the police in  carrying out specific policy directives.
SOC*3750.Restriction: Registration in BA.ANTH, BA.CJPP, BA.SOC (major, minor or area of concentration).
SOC*3750.Requisites:
(SOAN*2112 or SOC*2700), SOAN*2120
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*3840.Title: SOC*3840 Seminar in Sociology (0.5 Credits)
SOC*3840.Description: This course will be offered as a structured  seminar on various topics depending upon the  interests of the faculty member teaching the  course. Topics will be announced and course  outlines will be available at course selection.  The availability of third and fourth year seminar  courses will vary. Students must check with the  Department of Sociology and Anthropology to see  when seminar courses are available.
SOC*3840.Requisites:
10.00 credits including (1 of SOAN*2112, SOC*2080,  SOC*2700), SOAN*2120
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*3850.Title: SOC*3850 Seminar in Sociology (0.5 Credits)
SOC*3850.Description: This course will be offered as a structured  seminar on various topics depending upon the  interests of the faculty member teaching the  course. Topics will be announced and course  outlines will be available at course selection.  The availability of third and fourth year seminar  courses will vary. Students must check with the  Department of Sociology and Anthropology to see  when seminar courses are available.
SOC*3850.Requisites:
10.00 credits including (1 of SOAN*2112, SOC*2080,  SOC*2700), SOAN*2120
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*3950.Title: SOC*3950 Special Projects in Sociology (0.5 Credits)
SOC*3950.Description: This special study option/reading course is  designed to provide advanced undergraduates with  an opportunity to explore independently the  frontiers and foundations of a field of  knowledge. Under supervision, the student will  study in greater depth topics related to regular  upper-level courses offered in the department  which the student has taken or is taking.  Permission of the instructor who will be  supervising the study is required.
SOC*3950.Restriction: Instructor consent required.  Please note, a student is allowed a total of 1.00  credits only for reading courses.
SOC*3950.Requisites:
10.00 credits
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4010.Title: SOC*4010 Violence and Society (0.5 Credits)
SOC*4010.Description: This course will focus on the changing nature of  violence in our society by critically evaluating  theory, research and public policy on the causes  and control of violence. The links among  structural, institutional and interpersonal  violence will be examined as well as the social  construction of violence, particularly why some  forms of violence are considered to be more  serious social problems than others.
SOC*4010.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH:CJPP, BAH:CJPP:C and BAH:SOC with an average of 70% in all course attempts in Sociology and Sociology and Anthropology courses. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4010.Requisites: 14.00 credits including (SOC*2700 or SOC*3310), (SOAN*3120  or POLS*3650 )   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4030.Title: SOC*4030 Advanced Topics in Criminology (0.5 Credits)
SOC*4030.Description: This is an in-depth study of selected issues in  criminology.
SOC*4030.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH:CJPP and BAH:CJPP:C. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4030.Requisites:
14.00 credits including (2 of SOC*3490, SOC*3710, SOC*3730,  SOC*3740, SOC*3750), (1 of ANTH*3690, SOC*2700, SOC*3310),  (SOAN*3120 or POLS*3650)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4130.Title: SOC*4130 Adv Sem in Violence & Society (1 Credits)
SOC*4130.Description: This advanced seminar offers an in-depth study of the nature of violence in our society.
SOC*4130.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH.CJPP, BAH.CJPP:C and BAH.SOC with an average of 70% in all course attempts in Sociology and Sociology and Anthropology courses. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4130.Requisites: 14.00 credits including (POLS*3650 or SOAN*3120), (SOC*2700 or SOC*3310)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4140.Title: SOC*4140 Victimology (1 Credits)
SOC*4140.Description: This course will focus on understanding the impact of crime, the needs of victims, and victims' experiences in the criminal justice system. Students will explore topics such as the social and media constructions of victimization and victimhood, victimological theories, gender and victimization, victimization in childhood and adolescence, physical and mental health outcomes of victimization, and resilience.
SOC*4140.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH.CJPP, BAH.CJPP:C and BAH.SOC with an average of 70% in all course attempts in Sociology and Sociology and Anthropology courses. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4140.Requisites: 14.00 credits including (POLS*3650 or SOAN*3120), (SOC*2700 or SOC*3310)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4150.Title: SOC*4150 Youth and Violence (1 Credits)
SOC*4150.Description: This course is a sociological exploration of youth violence, considering current explanations of youth violence, the sociological implications of Canada's juvenile justice system and policies impacting youth, and the influence of media, family and school. Reform initiatives and justice alternatives aimed at youth will also be examined.
SOC*4150.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH.CJPP, BAH.CJPP:C and BAH.SOC with an average of 70% in all course attempts in Sociology and Sociology and Anthropology courses. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4150.Requisites: 14.00 credits including (POLS*3650 or SOAN*3120), (SOC*2700 or SOC*3310)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4170.Title: SOC*4170 Viol Against Women/Gendered (1 Credits)
SOC*4170.Description: This course examines the premise that violence against women and gendered violence are the products of historical and institutional inequalities linked to structural and symbolic processes, and will pay attention to the role of gender not as an identity, but as a social structure that intersects with other structures of inequality.
SOC*4170.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH.CJPP, BAH.CJPP:C and BAH.SOC with an average of 70% in all course attempts in Sociology and Sociology and Anthropology courses. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4170.Requisites: 14.00 credits including (POLS*3650 or SOAN*3120), (SOC*2700 or SOC*3310)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4200.Title: SOC*4200 Advanced Topics in Criminal Ju (0.5 Credits)
SOC*4200.Description: This is an in-depth study of issues in criminal  justice.
SOC*4200.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH:CJPP and BAH:CJPP:C. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4200.Requisites:
14.00 credits including (2 of SOC*3490, SOC*3710, SOC*3730,  SOC*3740, SOC*3750), (1 of ANTH*3690, SOC*2700, SOC*3310),  (SOAN*3120 or POLS*3650)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4300.Title: SOC*4300 Theoretical & Method. Issues (0.5 Credits)
SOC*4300.Description: This course will provide an opportunity for  sociology majors to consider in detail the  integration of theoretical and methodological  issues at an advanced level. It is meant to  engage students in the latest developments in a  particular area of the discipline. Course topics  will be announced and course outlines will be  available at course selection time. This course  is highly recommended to students who are  considering graduate work in sociology.
SOC*4300.Requisites:
14.00 credits including SOAN*3070, SOAN*3120, SOC*3310
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4320.Title: SOC*4320 Adv Sem in Criminal Justice (1 Credits)
SOC*4320.Description: This advanced seminar offers an in-depth study of issues in criminal justice.
SOC*4320.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH.CJPP and BAH.CJPP:C. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4320.Requisites: 14.00 credits including (POLS*3650 or SOAN*3120), (1 of ANTH*3690, SOC*2700, SOC*3310), (2 of SOC*3490, SOC*3710, SOC*3730, SOC*3740, SOC*3750)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4330.Title: SOC*4330 Miscarriages of Justice (1 Credits)
SOC*4330.Description: This course will explore procedures used by various criminal justice actors to assess their potential for producing errors in justice, consider the implications of balancing the rights of the accused with crime control, and discuss existing redress mechanisms to remedy miscarriages of justice and provide suggestions for policy change. Students will consider the psychological, familial, emotional, and economic consequences of wrongful convictions.
SOC*4330.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH.CJPP and BAH.CJPP:C. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4330.Requisites: 14.00 credits including (POLS*3650 or SOAN*3120), (1 of ANTH*3690, SOC*2700, SOC*3310), (2 of SOC*3490, SOC*3710, SOC*3730, SOC*3740, SOC*3750)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4340.Title: SOC*4340 Women & Criminal Justice Sys (1 Credits)
SOC*4340.Description: This course will critically examine selective issues related to the way women (including young women) as offenders, victims/survivors, and practitioners/professionals in the criminal justice system are theorized, researched, represented in media and attended to in policy and practice. Students will consider the role of age, race, class, gender, abilities, sexualities and the media in the shaping of public opinion and public policy about women and crime.
SOC*4340.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH.CJPP and BAH.CJPP:C. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4340.Requisites: 14.00 credits including (POLS*3650 or SOAN*3120), (1 of ANTH*3690, SOC*2700, SOC*3310), (2 of SOC*3490, SOC*3710, SOC*3730, SOC*3740, SOC*3750)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4350.Title: SOC*4350 Drugs and Society (1 Credits)
SOC*4350.Description: This course will examine sociological perspectives on substance use behaviour and related policy discussions about drugs. Students will examine theoretical and substantive contributions on an array of topics-from the concept of addiction to historical and recent experiences of users of a variety of drugs.
SOC*4350.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH.CJPP and BAH.CJPP:C. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4350.Requisites: 14.00 credits including (POLS*3650 or SOAN*3120),  (1 of ANTH*3690, SOC*2700, SOC*3310), (2 of SOC*3490, SOC*3710, SOC*3730, SOC*3740, SOC*3750)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4410.Title: SOC*4410 Women, Work & Public Policy (0.5 Credits)
SOC*4410.Description: In this course students will critically assess  the transformation of women's work in  contemporary society. A range of topics  pertaining to women's work will be explored with  particular attention paid to the processes  through which class, gender, race, ethnicity, and  age shape divisions of work. The course will also  focus on theories that have attempted to explain  the transformation of women's work.
SOC*4410.Requisites: 12.50 credits including (1 of ANTH*2160, ANTH*2180, IDEV*2000, SOAN*2112, SOC*2700), (1 of GEOG*2260, POLS*2650, SOAN*2120)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4420.Title: SOC*4420 Sociology of Food (0.5 Credits)
SOC*4420.Description: This course is directed towards upper level  students in sociology and related disciplines who  wish to consider the variety of contentious  issues surrounding food in the contemporary  world. The course will encourage a sociological  approach to food systems that is both  historically informed and comparative in scope.
SOC*4420.Requisites: 12.50 credits including (1 of GEOG*2260, IDEV*2100, POLS*2650, SOAN*2120, SOAN*3070), (1 of ANTH*2160, ANTH*2180, IDEV*2000, IDEV*2300, SOAN*2112)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4430.Title: SOC*4430 Alt Social Possibilities (0.5 Credits)
SOC*4430.Description: This course uses the full range of sociological  theory to suggest what alternative ways of  organizing society might be possible. Students  will examine different accounts of theories of  why outcomes are not equal from functionalist  theories of stratification to theories of class  domination and exploitation to economic market  accounts to feminist accounts based on  patriarchy. This course will allow students to  bring together for themselves a wide range of  theories used in other courses and apply them to  how their own ideals might be implemented.
SOC*4430.Requisites:
12.50 credits including (1 of ANTH*3690, SOC*2700,  SOC*3310), (1 of POLS*2650, POLS*3180, SOAN*2120)
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4460.Title: SOC*4460 Adv Sem in Criminology (1 Credits)
SOC*4460.Description: This advanced seminar offers an in-depth study of selected issues in criminology.
SOC*4460.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH.CJPP and BAH.CJPP:C. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4460.Requisites: 14.00 credits including (POLS*3650 or SOAN*3120), (1 of ANTH*3690, SOC*2700, SOC*3310), (2 of SOC*3490, SOC*3710, SOC*3730, SOC*3740, SOC*3750)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4470.Title: SOC*4470 Youth in Conflict with Law (1 Credits)
SOC*4470.Description: This course offers an in-depth, critical analysis of youth crime and deviance. The purpose of the course is to provide students with an up-to-date overview of sociological theory and empirical research in the field of youth crime and social/criminal justice policy.
SOC*4470.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH.CJPP and BAH.CJPP:C. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4470.Requisites: 14.00 credits including (POLS*3650 or SOAN*3120), (1 of ANTH*3690, SOC*2700, SOC*3310),  (2 of SOC*3490, SOC*3710, SOC*3730, SOC*3740, SOC*3750)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4480.Title: SOC*4480 Moral Regulation (1 Credits)
SOC*4480.Description: This course introduces students to contemporary literature and critical perspectives on the evolving concept of moral regulation by examining theoretical and substantive contributions, with particular attention to Canadian examples. Potential topics of discussion include sexual behaviour, drug consumption, public health, and the moral regulation of the poor.
SOC*4480.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH.CJPP and BAH.CJPP:C. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4480.Requisites: 14.00 credits including (POLS*3650 or SOAN*3120), (1 of ANTH*3690, SOC*2700, SOC*3310), (2 of SOC*3490, SOC*3710, SOC*3730, SOC*3740, SOC*3750)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4490.Title: SOC*4490 Adv Theory & Methods in Crim (1 Credits)
SOC*4490.Description: This course is designed to teach students how to test criminological theory with self-report survey data. Special attention will be given to the conceptual logic involved in linking theory with data, in addition to understanding the technical skills that are required to undertake this approach to criminological research.
SOC*4490.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH.CJPP and BAH.CJPP:C. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4490.Requisites: 14.00 credits including (POLS*3650 or SOAN*3120),  (1 of ANTH*3690, SOC*2700, SOC*3310), (2 of SOC*3490, SOC*3710, SOC*3730, SOC*3740, SOC*3750)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4500.Title: SOC*4500 Crime and Social Exclusion (1 Credits)
SOC*4500.Description: This course is designed to introduce students to the ways in which socially excluded populations (e.g., homeless people) encounter the criminal justice system. Students will review a range of topics, statistical trends, and theory and research on the ways in which socially excluded groups come into contact with the police, courts and correctional system.
SOC*4500.Restriction: Restricted to students in BAH.CJPP and BAH.CJPP:C. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4500.Requisites: 14.00 credits including (POLS*3650 or SOAN*3120), (1 of ANTH*3690, SOC*2700, SOC*3310), (2 of SOC*3490, SOC*3710, SOC*3730, SOC*3740, SOC*3750)   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4740.Description: This course will be offered as a structured  seminar on various topics depending upon the  interests of the faculty member teaching the  course. 12.50 credits including SOC*3310, SOAN*3070, SOAN*3120

SOC*4900.Title: SOC*4900 Honours Sociology Thesis I (0.5 Credits)
SOC*4900.Description: Development and design of an honours thesis  proposal conducted under the supervision of a  faculty member. Recommended to Honours students.
SOC*4900.Restriction: A cumulative average of 75% in all Sociology and Anthropology courses. Instructor consent required. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4900.Requisites:
15.00 credits including SOC*3310, SOAN*3070, SOAN*3120.  CJPP students must have 15.00 credits including SOC*2700,  SOAN*3120, or POLS*3650
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SOC*4910.Title: SOC*4910 Honours Sociology Thesis II (0.5 Credits)
SOC*4910.Description: Completion and presentation of honours thesis.
SOC*4910.Restriction: Instructor consent required. CJPP and CJPP:C students are restricted to a maximum of 3.00 credits in SOC and POLS 4000-level CJPP restricted electives.
SOC*4910.Requisites:
SOC*4900
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SPAN*1100.Title: SPAN*1100 Introductory Spanish I (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*1100.Description: This course introduces students to the basics of spoken and written Spanish through the study of grammar, vocabulary and culture. The course is for students with no previous studies in Spanish.
SPAN*1100.Offering: Also offered through Distance  Education format.
SPAN*1100.Restriction: This course is not intended for students with prior knowledge in Spanish. Students with previous knowledge in the language must seek advice on course selection from the Head of Spanish and Hispanic Studies and might be assigned to another level of Spanish.

SPAN*1110.Title: SPAN*1110 Introductory Spanish II (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*1110.Description: This is a continuation of SPAN*1100. Students will develop and apply increased reading, writing, listening and oral skills in Spanish through the study of new vocabulary, grammatical structures and culture.
SPAN*1110.Requisites: SPAN*1100   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SPAN*1500.Title: SPAN*1500 Hispanic Film (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*1500.Description: This course, taught in English, introduces students to cinema in the Hispanic world. Students will examine major works in the Hispanic cinematic tradition. Depending on the instructor, Spanish-language films from Spain, South America, Central America, the Caribbean, the United States, the Philippines or Africa may be included. Themes discussed will include the historical and artistic contexts in which the films were released, the economic and political difficulties facing film production and distribution, censorship, competition from Hollywood, concepts of genre, ideological commitment and the role of the director as well as issues such as poverty, migration, ethnic difference, political conflict and the roles of women and sexual and gender minorities.

SPAN*2000.Title: SPAN*2000 Intermediate Spanish I (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*2000.Description: This course is for students who have completed  either first year University Spanish or 4U  Spanish as well as for those who are heritage  speakers. This course examines cultural topics  and grammatical structures in greater depth while  focusing on vocabulary acquisition, and  development of oral, written, and listening  skills.

SPAN*2010.Title: SPAN*2010 Intermediate Spanish II (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*2010.Description: Students will acquire and apply improved skills  in reading, writing, and conversation through  further study of grammar and culture. The course  encourages students to enhance their analytical  and linguistic skills through the use of  appropriate structures as they formulate and  support opinions.
SPAN*2010.Requisites: SPAN*2000   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SPAN*2040.Title: SPAN*2040 Culture of Spain (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*2040.Description: This course is an examination of the historical  and cultural events that provided the background  for the development of modern Spain, as well as a  visual survey of Spanish culture.
SPAN*2040.Requisites:
HISP*1110 or SPAN*1110
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SPAN*2990.Title: SPAN*2990 Hispanic Literary Studies (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*2990.Description: This course is an introduction to literary  studies in Spanish. The course focuses on  critical terminology and methods through a  selection of prose, poetry and drama from Spain  and Spanish America.
SPAN*2990.Requisites:
HISP*1110 or SPAN*1110
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SPAN*3080.Title: SPAN*3080 Spanish American Culture (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*3080.Description: This course is a survey through selected  readings, class discussion and audio-visual  materials of the Spanish American countries,  their histories, society, institutions and  culture.
SPAN*3080.Requisites:
HISP*2000 or SPAN*2000
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SPAN*3210.Title: SPAN*3210 Topics in Hispanic Studies (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*3210.Description: This course, taught in Spanish, with texts in the  original language, provides an intensive study of  a specific aspect of Hispanic Studies.
SPAN*3210.Requisites: 1 of SPAN*2990, SPAN*3220, SPAN*3230   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SPAN*3220.Title: SPAN*3220 Literature and Arts I (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*3220.Description: This course will be taught in Spanish, with texts  studied in the original language, and provides a  detailed examination of a theme, period or  movement in the literature and/or arts of Spain.
SPAN*3220.Requisites:
HISP*2990 or SPAN*2990
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SPAN*3230.Title: SPAN*3230 Literature and Arts II (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*3230.Description: This course will be taught in Spanish, with texts  studied in the original language, and provides a  detailed examination of a theme, period or  movement in the literature and/or arts of Latin  America.
SPAN*3230.Requisites:
HISP*2990 or SPAN*2990
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SPAN*3240.Title: SPAN*3240 Topics in Hispanic Linguistics (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*3240.Description: This course offers an introduction to linguistic  topics including history of the Spanish language,  language variation and change, and Spanish  phonetics, which may vary from year to year.
SPAN*3240.Requisites:
HISP*1110 or SPAN*1110
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SPAN*3500.Title: SPAN*3500 Advanced Spanish I (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*3500.Description: This is an advanced language course that focuses  on the refinement of students' written and verbal  communication skills in Spanish.
SPAN*3500.Requisites:
HISP*2010 or SPAN*2010
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SPAN*3700.Title: SPAN*3700 Experiential Learning & Lang (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*3700.Description: This course provides an opportunity for  independent study based on an experiential  project in Spanish or Hispanic Studies. The  project (approximately 70 hours) must be approved  by a faculty member in the School of Languages  and Literatures. It will include research about  experiential learning, a reflective piece of  writing and a public oral presentation about the  project.
SPAN*3700.Offering: Also offered through  Distance Education format.
SPAN*3700.Restriction: A  minimum cumulative average of 70% in all Spanish  course attempts. Instructor consent  required.
SPAN*3700.Requisites:
10.00 credits including 1.50 credits in Spanish.
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SPAN*3800.Title: SPAN*3800 Directed Readings in Hisp Stud (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*3800.Description: A reading course in Spanish or Spanish American  literature designed according to the previous  studies and the interests of the individual  student. Normally, students will not be permitted  to take more than two courses in the Directed  Readings sequence.
SPAN*3800.Requisites:
1.00 credits from the following: (HISP*3220 or SPAN*3220),  (HISP*3230 or SPAN*3230), SPAN*3080
   - Must be completed prior to taking this course.

SPAN*3810.Title: SPAN*3810 Directed Readings in Hisp Stud (0.5 Credits)
SPAN*3810.Description: A reading course in Spanish or Spanish American  literature designed according to the previous  studies and the interests of the individual  student. Normally, students will not be permitted  to take more than two courses in the Directed  Readings sequence.
SPAN*3810.Requisites:
1.00 credits from the following: (HISP*3220 or SPAN*3220),  (HISP*3230 or SPAN*3230), SPAN*3080
